definition_zh: 社会与文化为男女分别规定的一整套行为、职责与期待
definition_en: the set of behaviours, duties and expectations that a society attaches to being a man or a woman
core_image: 同一间屋子里摆着两套不同的工牌，一套写着照料，一套写着供养，进门的人被悄悄分到其中一边
scene: 老照片里的厨房与车间各站着一排人，谁该去哪里早已被安排好。In many villages, gender roles still decide who cooks and who ploughs.
sceneCN: 这里 gender roles 指「社会按性别分派给男女的行为与职责」（第 1 个义项：一整套被社会期待的行为规范）；句意为在许多村庄里，性别角色仍然决定谁做饭、谁耕地。可辨识物件：老照片、灶台、犁、围裙、车间。

pos.zh: 性别角色（复数名词短语）
社会性别分工（社会学用语）

senses.title: Social expectations attached to sex
senses.titleCN: 社会按性别规定的行为期待
senses.definition: the package of behaviours and duties that a society treats as proper for each sex
senses.definitionCN: 社会认为每种性别应当具备的一整套行为与职责
senses.example: In many villages, gender roles still decide who cooks and who ploughs.
senses.exampleCN: 在许多村庄里，性别角色仍然决定谁做饭、谁耕地。
senses.why: gender comes from Latin genus 'kind', and role from rotulus, the little roll that held an actor's part, so the phrase treats sex as a part one is cast in.
senses.whyCN: gender 来自拉丁 genus「种类」，role 来自写有演员台词的 rotulus「小卷纸」，因此这个短语把性别当作被分派的角色。

senses.title: Division of household labour
senses.titleCN: 家务与育儿中的性别分工
senses.definition: the assignment of cooking, cleaning and childcare to one sex within the home
senses.definitionCN: 在家庭内部把做饭、清洁与照护分派给某一种性别
senses.example: The survey found gender roles giving women the cooking and men the repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 调查发现，性别角色把做饭交给女性，把修理交给男性。
senses.why: the household is the first place where an abstract expectation turns into visible daily work.
senses.whyCN: 家庭是抽象期待变成可见日常劳动的第一个场所。

senses.title: Segregation in paid work
senses.titleCN: 有偿劳动中的性别分隔
senses.definition: the steering of men and women into different jobs and different pay grades
senses.definitionCN: 把男女分别导向不同职业与不同薪酬等级的做法
senses.example: Factory records show gender roles pushing women into the sewing rooms.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂档案显示，性别角色把女性推入缝纫车间。
senses.why: industry repeated the household split on a larger scale, and the same phrase moved with it.
senses.whyCN: 工业把家庭里的分工在更大尺度上重演，同一个短语也随之迁移。

senses.title: Gendered paths through school
senses.titleCN: 教育分流中的性别倾向
senses.definition: the tendency of teachers and materials to direct pupils of each sex toward different subjects
senses.definitionCN: 教师与教材把不同性别的学生导向不同学科的倾向
senses.example: Teachers once let gender roles push girls away from physics.
senses.exampleCN: 教师曾任由性别角色把女生挡在物理之外。
senses.why: schooling passes on expectations before anyone enters the labour market.
senses.whyCN: 学校教育在进入劳动力市场之前就传递了这些期待。

senses.title: Unequal access to public office
senses.titleCN: 公共职位与领导权的性别差异
senses.definition: the pattern by which one sex is expected to speak in public and hold office while the other is not
senses.definitionCN: 一种性别被期待公开发言并担任公职、另一种则不然的格局
senses.example: Voting rules and gender roles long kept women off the council.
senses.exampleCN: 选举规则与性别角色长期把女性挡在议事会之外。
senses.why: public power is the arena where a private expectation becomes a structural barrier.
senses.whyCN: 公共权力是私人期待变成结构性障碍的场所。

senses.title: Roles that shift with history
senses.titleCN: 随历史条件变化的性别分工
senses.definition: the rearrangement of who does what when war, migration or industry changes the supply of labour
senses.definitionCN: 战争、迁徙或工业改变劳动力供给时，谁做什么随之重新安排
senses.example: Wartime industry overturned gender roles for a few years.
senses.exampleCN: 战时工业在几年间颠覆了性别角色。
senses.why: when labour is scarce, an arrangement that looked natural is suddenly shown to be a decision.
senses.whyCN: 劳动力短缺时，看似自然的分工立刻显出它只是人为安排。

senses.title: How children learn the part
senses.titleCN: 性别角色的社会化过程
senses.definition: the process by which toys, praise and punishment teach a child which part to play
senses.definitionCN: 玩具、夸奖与责罚教会孩子该扮演哪个角色的过程
senses.example: Toys and praise teach gender roles long before children can name them.
senses.exampleCN: 玩具与夸奖在孩子会用词之前很久就教会了他们性别角色。
senses.why: the phrase is a script learned by imitation, not a trait present at birth.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语所指的是一套通过模仿习得的脚本，而非与生俱来的特质。

senses.title: Contesting and rewriting the script
senses.titleCN: 对性别角色的质疑与重构
senses.definition: the public argument over whether the assigned parts should be kept, revised or abolished
senses.definitionCN: 围绕既定角色应当保留、修改还是废除而展开的公共争论
senses.example: The campaign asked voters to reject gender roles written into labour law.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动要求选民否决写进劳动法里的性别角色。
senses.why: once an arrangement is named as a role, it can be argued with and rewritten.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某种安排被命名为角色，它就可以被争论和改写。

intro.en: Gender roles is a modern English phrase joining gender, from Latin genus 'kind, sort' through Old French, and role, from Latin rotulus 'little roll', the scroll on which an actor's part was written. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: gender roles 是现代英语短语，由 gender 与 role 合成：gender 经古法语来自拉丁 genus「种类」，role 来自拉丁 rotulus「小卷纸」，原指写着演员台词的纸卷。年代均为约数。

items.en: Genus meant 'kind, sort, race' and had the stem gener-. Its deeper origin is generally traced to the same root as gignere 'to beget', though the pre-Latin shape is a reconstruction rather than a witnessed form.
items.cn: genus 意为「种类、类别、族类」，词干为 gener-。其更深来源一般认为与 gignere「生育」同根，但拉丁语之前的形态属重构形式，并无实际书证。

items.en: Old French gendre, later genre, carried the noun into English, where it first meant 'kind, sort' and only later named a class of nouns in grammar.
items.cn: 古法语 gendre（后作 genre）把这个名词带入英语，最初意为「种类」，后来才指语法中的名词类别。

items.en: Rotulus, a diminutive of rota 'wheel', named a small roll of paper; an actor's part copied on such a roll gave Old French rolle and English role.
items.cn: rotulus 是 rota「轮子」的指小形式，指小卷纸；抄在这种纸卷上的演员台词，衍生出古法语 rolle 与英语 role。

items.en: English joined the two nouns in the mid-twentieth century, when social science needed a neutral term for the part a society assigns to each sex.
items.cn: 英语在二十世纪中叶把这两个名词组合起来，当时社会科学需要一个中性词来指社会分派给每种性别的角色。

items.en: From the 1970s the plural phrase spread into law, education and development policy, where it usually names a pattern to be measured rather than a rule to be praised.
items.cn: 从二十世纪七十年代起，这个复数短语进入法律、教育与发展政策，通常指一种可被测量的格局，而非一种值得称赞的规则。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): no single first printed use of the plural phrase is recorded, and the pre-Latin shape of genus is reconstructed, so any proposed older form is not attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个复数短语没有确切的最早印刷书证；genus 在拉丁语之前的形态属重构形式，任何提出的更早形式都无实际书证。

note.en: Group one holds words built from the same two Latin stocks; group two holds terms that describe the same social arrangement from another angle.
note.cn: 第一组是同出这两个拉丁词干的词；第二组是从另一个角度描述同一社会安排的词。

entries.definition: The noun for the social or grammatical category; gender roles is the set of parts assigned to that category.
entries.definitionCN: 指社会或语法类别的名词；gender roles 则是分派给这一类别的整套角色。

entries.definition: A single part played in a setting; the phrase pluralises it into a whole package.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某一情境中扮演的单个角色；这个短语把它复数化为一整套。

entries.definition: Also from Latin genus, but it names a literary kind, not a social one.
entries.definitionCN: 同样来自拉丁 genus，但指文学类别，而非社会类别。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning marked by gender; it describes the result of roles rather than the roles themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「带性别色彩的」形容词；描述角色的结果，而非角色本身。

entries.definition: An older term that stresses biological sex; gender roles stresses the social assignment instead.
entries.definitionCN: 较早的同义词，强调生理性别；gender roles 则强调社会分派。

entries.definition: The general split of tasks in a group; it becomes gender roles only when the split follows sex.
entries.definitionCN: 指群体中任务的一般划分；只有当划分依照性别时，才成为性别角色。

entries.definition: Widely held simplified images of a group; they justify roles but are not the roles themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 对某群体广泛持有的简化印象；它们为角色辩护，但本身不是角色。

entries.definition: Shared rules of behaviour; roles are the positions to which those rules are attached.
entries.definitionCN: 共享的行为规则；角色则是这些规则所依附的位置。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: gender comes from Latin genus 'kind', so a gender role is the kind of part one is cast in.
normal.cn: gender 来自拉丁 genus「种类」，因此性别角色就是被分派去演的那一类角色。

normal.en: role comes from rotulus, the little paper roll that held an actor's lines.
normal.cn: role 来自 rotulus，即写着演员台词的小纸卷。

normal.en: The phrase is usually plural because each person carries several parts at once.
normal.cn: 这个短语通常用复数，因为每个人同时承担好几个角色。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the debate: traditional gender roles, rigid gender roles, reverse gender roles.
normal.cn: 争论中的固定搭配：传统性别角色、僵化的性别角色、性别角色反转。

normal.en: The related adjective is gendered, as in a gendered division of labour.
normal.cn: 相关形容词是 gendered，如「带性别色彩的分工」。

abstract.en: Picture a theatre where the script was written before the actors were born.
abstract.cn: 想象一座剧场，剧本在演员出生之前就已写好。

abstract.en: Picture two doors marked only by the work waiting behind them.
abstract.cn: 想象两扇门，门上只写着门后等着的工作。

abstract.en: Picture a map whose roads were drawn by someone else's hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，上面的路是别人替你画的。

examples.en: Census data show gender roles shaping who leaves work to care for children.
examples.cn: 人口普查数据显示，性别角色决定了谁辞职在家照看孩子。

examples.en: The new syllabus asks students to trace gender roles across three generations.
examples.cn: 新教学大纲要求学生追溯三代人之中的性别角色变化。

examples.en: When the factory reopened, gender roles in the town had quietly reversed.
examples.cn: 工厂重新开工时，镇上的性别角色已悄然反转。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「gender（性别）+ roles（角色）」——社会给男女各发一张角色卡

root: gender 来自拉丁 genus「种类、族类」，词干 gener-，经古法语 gendre 进入英语；role 来自拉丁 rotulus「小卷纸」，原指写着演员台词的纸卷，经古法语 rolle。更早的印欧形式均属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a society writes a part for each sex, and that part is then performed at home, at school, at work, in public office, and finally questioned and rewritten.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：社会为每种性别写好一个角色，这个角色再依次在家庭、学校、职场、公共职位上演出，最后被质疑与改写。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two sets of name tags lie on one table, and each newcomer is quietly handed one of them.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上放着两套工牌，每个新来的人都被悄悄递上其中一套。

branches.en: THE SCRIPT ITSELF: the phrase names an expectation before it names any workplace.
branches.cn: 脚本本身：这个短语先指一套期待，再指任何具体场所。

branches.en: LEARNING AT HOME: the household is where the script is first performed and first taught.
branches.cn: 在家中习得：家庭既是脚本首次上演之处，也是它首次被传授之处。

branches.en: TRAINING AND EARNING: school and paid work sort people along the same line.
branches.cn: 受训与谋生：学校与有偿劳动沿同一条界线分流人群。

branches.en: PUBLIC POWER: the line becomes heaviest where decisions are made.
branches.cn: 公共权力：在决策所在之处，这条界线也最沉重。

branches.en: A SCRIPT THAT MOVES: scarcity rewrites it, and naming it lets people argue back.
branches.cn: 会移动的脚本：匮乏会改写它，而命名它则让人得以反驳。

intro.en: The phrase is built from two nouns whose stems and suffixes also build a family of related English words, so it can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个名词构成，它们的词干与后缀还构成一族相关英语词，因此可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin genus supplied the gender family and Latin rotulus supplied the role family; the suffix -ed later turned gender into an adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 genus 衍生出 gender 一族，拉丁 rotulus 衍生出 role 一族；后缀 -ed 后来又把 gender 变成形容词。

items.structure: gen- (Latin root, as in genus, generis)
items.example: The root runs through the whole gender family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根贯穿整个 gender 词族。

items.example: Genus named a class before it named a sex.
items.exampleCN: genus 先指一个类别，后来才与性别相关。

items.example: The same root names a literary genre.
items.exampleCN: 同一个词根也指文学体裁。

items.meaning: kind; then grammatical class; then social sex
items.meaningCN: 种类；语法类别；社会性别
items.example: Gender shifted from grammar to social life.
items.exampleCN: gender 从语法领域移入社会生活。

items.example: Rota is the base of the little roll.
items.exampleCN: rota 是那个小卷纸的词源基础。

items.structure: rotulus, rotuli (Latin noun, diminutive of rota)
items.example: An actor's part was copied onto a rotulus.
items.exampleCN: 演员的台词被抄在一卷小纸上。

items.example: The roll of paper gave the player a role.
items.exampleCN: 那卷纸给了演员一个角色。

items.example: Gendered work is work marked by gender.
items.exampleCN: gendered work 即带性别标记的工作。

items.meaning: the parts assigned to each sex
items.meaningCN: 分派给每种性别的角色
items.example: The plural marks the whole package, not one task.
items.exampleCN: 复数标记的是整套角色，而非单项任务。

items.meaning: acting out a part in training
items.example: Role-play lets learners rehearse a part safely.
items.exampleCN: 角色扮演让学习者在安全情境中演练某个角色。

latinEntries.structure: rotulus, rotuli (m., second declension; diminutive of rota)

definition_zh: 由血缘与婚姻关系连接起来、可以互相往来的亲属群体
definition_en: the web of relatives linked by blood or marriage through whom people exchange help, information and obligations
core_image: 一张手绘的族谱铺在桌上，线条从一对老人向四周伸开，每个节点都连着另一户人家的门
scene: 祠堂的墙上挂着一张很大的族谱，红线和黑线把几十户人家连在一起。A kinship network links these farmers to cousins in three neighbouring counties.
sceneCN: 这里 kinship network 指「由血缘与婚姻连接、可彼此往来的亲属群体」（第 1 个义项：一张以亲属关系为线的互助之网）；句意为这张亲属网络把这些农户与三个邻县的表亲连在一起。可辨识物件：族谱、红线、黑线、祠堂、门牌。

pos.zh: 人类学中的亲属关系体系

senses.title: Relatives linked by blood or marriage
senses.titleCN: 由血缘或婚姻连接的亲属整体
senses.definition: the whole set of relatives connected to a person through descent or marriage
senses.definitionCN: 通过血缘或婚姻与某人连在一起的全部亲属
senses.example: Anthropologists mapped the kinship network before asking about land use.
senses.exampleCN: 人类学家先画出亲属网络，再询问土地利用情况。
senses.why: kin names the family stock, and network turns it into a set of links rather than a list of names.
senses.whyCN: kin 指家族血脉，network 则把它变成一组联结，而非一串名字。

senses.title: The extended family beyond the household
senses.titleCN: 超出小家庭的扩展亲属
senses.definition: the relatives who live outside one's own house but remain part of daily obligation
senses.definitionCN: 不住在自己家中、却仍属日常义务范围的亲属
senses.example: A child in that village is raised by the wider kinship network.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个村庄里，孩子由更广的亲属网络共同抚养。
senses.why: a household is small, and the network is precisely what lies beyond its walls.
senses.whyCN: 家庭很小，而亲属网络恰恰指墙外的那些关系。

senses.title: A system of kinship terms
senses.definition: the set of words a language uses to distinguish cousins, in-laws and generations
senses.definitionCN: 一种语言用来区分表亲、姻亲与辈分的整套称谓
senses.example: The language encodes the kinship network in separate words for cross-cousins.
senses.exampleCN: 这种语言用不同的词称呼交叉表亲，把亲属网络编进词汇。
senses.why: terms are the map a society draws of its own links.
senses.whyCN: 称谓是社会为自己那些联结画出的地图。

senses.title: A source of everyday support
senses.titleCN: 日常互助与照护的来源
senses.definition: the flow of food, labour and care that relatives give one another in hard times
senses.definitionCN: 困难时期亲属之间输送食物、劳力与照护的流动
senses.example: When the harvest failed, the kinship network supplied grain and labour.
senses.exampleCN: 收成失败时，亲属网络提供了粮食与劳力。
senses.why: links are kept alive by use, so support is the working part of the network.
senses.whyCN: 联结靠使用而存活，因此互助就是这张网真正运转的部分。

senses.title: A channel for inheritance and ritual duty
senses.titleCN: 继承与仪式义务的通道
senses.definition: the route along which property, names and ritual obligations pass from one generation to the next
senses.definitionCN: 财产、名分与仪式义务代代相传所沿的路径
senses.example: Ritual obligations pass along the kinship network rather than the household.
senses.exampleCN: 仪式义务沿着亲属网络传递，而不是沿家庭传递。
senses.why: inheritance and rites are where links become legally and morally binding.
senses.whyCN: 继承与仪式正是联结获得法律与道德约束力的地方。

senses.title: A route for jobs, loans and news
senses.titleCN: 求职、借贷与消息的渠道
senses.definition: the use of relatives as trusted contacts for employment, credit and information
senses.definitionCN: 把亲属当作求职、信贷与消息的可信联系人
senses.example: Migrants found work through a kinship network rather than an agency.
senses.exampleCN: 外来务工者通过亲属网络而非中介找到工作。
senses.why: a web of trusted ties moves resources that formal institutions cannot reach.
senses.whyCN: 由信任联结成的网能输送正式机构触及不到的资源。

senses.title: A web that shrinks in cities
senses.titleCN: 城市化中收缩的亲属网络
senses.definition: the thinning of regular contact among relatives under long commutes and rented flats
senses.definitionCN: 在长途通勤与租住公寓条件下亲属往来逐渐变稀
senses.example: Flat doors and long commutes leave the kinship network thin.
senses.exampleCN: 单元门与长途通勤使亲属网络变得稀薄。
senses.why: distance and time cost links, and a network with no visits fades.
senses.whyCN: 距离与时间消耗联结，无人走访的网络会逐渐消失。

senses.title: Links kept across borders
senses.definition: the maintenance of family ties by phone, remittance and return visits after migration
senses.definitionCN: 迁移之后靠电话、汇款与回乡探访维持的家庭关系
senses.example: Phone calls and remittances hold the kinship network across two continents.
senses.exampleCN: 电话与汇款把亲属网络维系在两个大陆之间。
senses.why: cheap communication lets an old web survive migration instead of breaking.
senses.whyCN: 廉价的通信让旧网在迁移中存续，而不是断裂。

intro.en: Kinship network joins two native Germanic words: kin, from Old English cynn 'family, race', and network, from net plus work. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: kinship network 由两个本族日耳曼语词合成：kin 来自古英语 cynn「家族、族类」，network 由 net 与 work 构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cynn meant 'family, race, kind' and is related to kind. The pre-Germanic shape is reconstructed, so the older form is not witnessed in any text.
items.cn: cynn 意为「家族、族类、种类」，与 kind 同源。日耳曼语之前的形态属重构形式，没有任何文本书证。

items.en: The suffix -scipe made abstract nouns of state or condition, giving kinship the sense 'the condition of being kin'.
items.cn: 后缀 -scipe 构成表状态或状况的抽象名词，使 kinship 获得「身为亲属的状态」之义。

items.en: Net(t) named a mesh of cords, and weorc named work or deed; the compound network first named a mesh of lines, then any connected set.
items.cn: net(t) 指绳线结成的网，weorc 指劳作或行为；复合词 network 先指线网，后指任何相互连接的一整套。

items.en: In the twentieth century network was applied to people, and kinship network named a web of relatives rather than a list of names.
items.cn: 二十世纪，network 被用于人，kinship network 由此指一张亲属之网，而非一串名字。

items.en: Social anthropology made the phrase a technical term for the links a society recognizes, uses and transmits.
items.cn: 社会人类学把这个短语变成术语，指一个社会所承认、使用并传递的联结。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Germanic origin): the older Germanic shape of cynn is reconstructed, and no single first use of the full phrase is recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定（日耳曼语之前的来源）：cynn 更早的日耳曼语形态属重构形式，整个短语也没有确切的最早书证。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like or are built from kin; group two holds terms for a family group organized on another principle.
note.cn: 第一组是形似 kin 或由 kin 构成的词；第二组是按另一种原则组织家庭群体的词。

entries.definition: Kin plus the collective suffix -red: the relatives taken together, often with a shared ancestor.
entries.definitionCN: kin 加集体后缀 -red：聚在一起、常共有一祖先的亲属。

entries.definition: The abstract relation of being kin; a kinship network is the concrete set of links built from it.
entries.definitionCN: 指身为亲属的抽象关系；亲属网络则是由此建成的具体联结集合。

entries.definition: Relationship through marriage rather than blood, from Latin affinis 'neighbouring'.
entries.definitionCN: 指因婚姻而非血缘形成的关系，来自拉丁 affinis「邻近的」。

entries.definition: A set of connected points of any kind; only the modifier kin makes it a family web.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何相互连接的点集；只有前面的 kin 才使它成为亲属之网。

entries.definition: The relatives beyond the nuclear household treated as one group; the network stresses how they are connected.
entries.definitionCN: 指核心家庭之外的亲属整体；网络一词强调他们如何相连。

entries.definition: A large group claiming descent from one ancestor, often with a common name; a network need not share a name.
entries.definitionCN: 指自称出自同一祖先的大型群体，常共用名号；亲属网络则不必共用名号。

entries.definition: A single traced line of ancestors and descendants; a network contains many such lines at once.
entries.definitionCN: 指一条可追溯的世代传承线；亲属网络同时包含多条这样的线。

entries.definition: A web of people linked by friendship, work or interest; kinship network limits the links to relatives.
entries.definitionCN: 指由友谊、工作或兴趣连成的人际网；亲属网络则把联结限定在亲属之间。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: kin is the family stock; -ship turns it into the state of being related.
normal.cn: kin 指家族血脉；-ship 把它变成「有亲属关系」这一状态。

normal.en: network is literally net plus work: a mesh that does the work of connecting people.
normal.cn: network 字面是 net 加 work：一张承担连接工作的网。

normal.en: The same kin root appears in kinsman, kinswoman and kinfolk.
normal.cn: 同一 kin 词根出现在 kinsman、kinswoman 与 kinfolk 中。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: dense kinship network, extended kinship network, kinship network support.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：稠密的亲属网络、扩展的亲属网络、亲属网络的支持。

normal.en: Anthropology uses the phrase for links that are recognized, not merely biological.
normal.cn: 人类学用这个短语指被社会承认的联结，而不只是生物学上的关系。

abstract.en: Picture a map where every road ends at someone's kitchen door.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，每条路的尽头都是某户人家的厨房门口。

abstract.en: Picture a rope bridge whose planks are visits, calls and shared meals.
abstract.cn: 想象一座绳桥，桥板是一次次走访、电话与共餐。

abstract.en: Picture a net that holds grain in a bad year and lets it travel in a good one.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网，荒年兜住粮食，丰年又让粮食流动。

examples.en: The kinship network decided who would host the wedding feast.
examples.cn: 亲属网络决定了由谁来承办婚宴。

examples.en: A dense kinship network can soften the shock of a factory closure.
examples.cn: 稠密的亲属网络能缓冲工厂倒闭带来的冲击。

examples.en: Researchers asked how migration had changed the kinship network.
examples.cn: 研究者询问迁徙如何改变了亲属网络。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「kin（亲属）+ ship（船/关系）+ net（网）」——亲属像一张大网上的船，彼此连着

root: kin 来自古英语 cynn「家族、族类」，与 kind 同源；-ship 来自古英语 -scipe，表状态；network 为 net「网」+ work「劳作」的英语复合词。日耳曼语之前的形态均属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one structure: a set of links created by blood and marriage, which is then read as a group, a vocabulary, a support system, an inheritance channel, a job market, a shrinking city web and a web stretched across borders.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个结构展开：由血缘与婚姻造成的一组联结，再依次被读作一个群体、一套称谓、一套互助系统、一条继承通道、一个求职渠道、一张城市中收缩的网，以及一张跨境的网。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand-drawn family tree lying on a table, every branch ending at another household's door.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张手绘族谱铺在桌上，每条分支的尽头都是另一户人家的门。

branches.en: THE WEB ITSELF: the phrase names the whole set of links before it names any use of them.
branches.cn: 网本身：这个短语先指全部联结，再指这些联结的任何用途。

branches.en: OUTSIDE THE WALL AND IN THE LANGUAGE: the same links appear as relatives beyond the house and as words for those relatives.
branches.cn: 墙外与语言中：同一组联结既表现为屋外的亲属，也表现为称呼他们的词。

branches.en: CARE AND TRANSMISSION: food and labour flow one way, names and duties the other.
branches.cn: 照护与传承：食物与劳力向一个方向流动，名分与义务向另一个方向流动。

branches.en: TRUST AS CAPITAL: relatives become references, lenders and messengers.
branches.cn: 信任作资本：亲属变成担保人、放贷者与传信人。

branches.en: DISTANCE TESTS THE WEB: the city thins it, and migration either breaks it or stretches it.
branches.cn: 距离考验这张网：城市使它变稀，迁徙则要么扯断它，要么把它拉长。

intro.en: Both halves of the phrase are native Germanic material, so the family is read through stems and suffixes rather than Latin roots.
intro.cn: 这个短语的两半都是本族日耳曼语材料，因此要按词干与后缀来读，而非按拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: No Latin borrowing stands behind this phrase; the morphemes are Old English, so no Latin source forms are recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 这个短语背后没有拉丁借词，其语素来自古英语，因此不列拉丁语源形式。

items.example: Cynn is the ancestor of kin and kind.
items.exampleCN: cynn 是 kin 与 kind 的祖先形式。

items.example: Kin can mean one relative or the whole family.
items.exampleCN: kin 既可指一位亲属，也可指整个家族。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into a state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成一种状态。

items.example: Kinship is the relation before it is an organisation.
items.exampleCN: kinship 先是关系，后才成为一种组织。

items.example: A net holds things by connecting them.
items.exampleCN: 网通过连接来兜住东西。

items.example: Weorc gives English work.
items.exampleCN: weorc 衍生出英语 work。

items.meaning: a connected mesh; later any linked set
items.meaningCN: 相连的网；后指任何互联集合
items.example: The compound moved from cords to people.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词从绳线扩展到了人。

items.example: Kinsman keeps the old root alive.
items.exampleCN: kinsman 让古老词根延续下来。

items.example: Networking applies the mesh image to careers.
items.exampleCN: networking 把网的形象用于职业关系。

definition_zh: 两个人依法律或习俗结成的夫妻关系，也指确立这种关系的婚礼
definition_en: the legally or socially recognized union of two people as spouses, and the ceremony that establishes it
core_image: 一张铺着红纸的桌上并排放着两只旧戒指、一份证书和一把新房钥匙
scene: 老屋的堂屋里点着两支红烛，墙上贴着一张写满吉利话的纸。Her grandparents' marriage began with a ceremony that lasted three days.
sceneCN: 这里 marriage 指「两人依俗结成的夫妻结合」（第 1 个义项：由仪式与公认确立的配偶关系）；句意为她祖父母的婚姻始于一场持续三天的婚礼。可辨识物件：红烛、喜字、戒指、证书、钥匙。

senses.title: The recognized union of spouses
senses.titleCN: 被法律或社会承认的夫妻结合
senses.definition: the state in which two people are legally or socially recognized as spouses
senses.definitionCN: 两个人被法律或社会承认为配偶的状态
senses.example: Their marriage was registered at the county office in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的婚姻是春天在县里登记的。
senses.why: from Latin maritus 'husband', the noun names the wedded state itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词来自拉丁 maritus「丈夫」，直接指已婚状态本身。

senses.title: The wedding ceremony itself
senses.definition: the event in which vows are exchanged and the union is publicly made
senses.definitionCN: 交换誓言并公开确立结合的那场活动
senses.example: The whole village came to the marriage and stayed for the feast.
senses.exampleCN: 全村人都来参加婚礼，并留下来吃喜宴。
senses.why: the event and the state share one word because the rite is what creates the relation.
senses.whyCN: 仪式与状态共用一个词，因为正是仪式造成了这层关系。

senses.title: The ongoing state of being wed
senses.definition: the daily condition of living as a married couple over many years
senses.definitionCN: 多年来作为夫妻共同生活的日常状态
senses.example: Thirty years of marriage had taught them how to argue without wounding.
senses.exampleCN: 三十年的婚姻教会他们如何争吵却不伤人。
senses.why: the noun covers duration, not only the moment of union.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词涵盖持续时间，而不只是结合的那一刻。

senses.title: A type of marriage system
senses.definition: a socially defined form such as monogamy or polygyny, studied as a rule of the group
senses.definitionCN: 如一夫一妻或一夫多妻这类被社会定义的制度，作为群体规则来研究
senses.example: The community practiced marriage between cross-cousins.
senses.exampleCN: 这个社群实行交叉表亲之间的婚姻。
senses.why: societies classify forms of union, and the same noun labels the type.
senses.whyCN: 社会会给结合形式分类，同一个名词也就用来指类型。

senses.title: A close alliance between things
senses.titleCN: 事物之间的紧密结合（比喻义）
senses.definition: a metaphor for two different elements joined so closely that neither keeps its old shape
senses.definitionCN: 比喻两种不同成分紧密结合，彼此都不再保持原样
senses.example: The album is a marriage of folk melody and electronic rhythm.
senses.exampleCN: 这张专辑是民歌曲调与电子节奏的结合。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the core idea of two parties becoming one.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了「两方成为一体」的核心意思。

senses.title: A card game of matching pairs
senses.definition: a card game in which players collect matching pairs, named after the paired union
senses.definitionCN: 玩家收集同名对子的一种纸牌游戏，因配对而成名
senses.example: The old men played marriage beside the stove all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 老人们整晚在炉边玩配对纸牌。
senses.why: the game is named for the matched pair, echoing the union sense.
senses.whyCN: 这种游戏因成对的牌而得名，与「结合」义呼应。

senses.title: A religious sacrament
senses.definition: the union regarded as a sacred vow rather than only a civil contract
senses.definitionCN: 被视为神圣誓约、而非仅是民事契约的结合
senses.example: The church treats marriage as a vow made before God.
senses.exampleCN: 教会把婚姻视为在神面前立下的誓约。
senses.why: religions read the union as sacred, adding a layer the law does not supply.
senses.whyCN: 宗教把这种结合读作神圣的，添加了法律不提供的一层。

senses.title: A political alliance between families
senses.definition: a union arranged to bind two families, courts or states rather than two individuals
senses.definitionCN: 为联结两个家族、宫廷或国家而非两个个人而安排的婚姻
senses.example: The treaty was sealed by a marriage between the two courts.
senses.exampleCN: 条约由两个宫廷之间的联姻加以巩固。
senses.why: kinship was once a diplomatic instrument, and the noun named that instrument.
senses.whyCN: 亲属关系曾是外交工具，这个词就指那件工具。

senses.title: The legal registration of the union
senses.titleCN: 婚姻的法律登记与效力
senses.definition: the recorded act that gives the union standing in courts and in inheritance law
senses.definitionCN: 使这种结合在法院与继承法中生效的登记行为
senses.example: Without registration, the marriage had no standing in court.
senses.exampleCN: 没有登记，这段婚姻在法庭上不具效力。
senses.why: modern states turn the relation into a recorded fact with legal consequences.
senses.whyCN: 现代国家把这种关系变成一项带有法律后果的登记事实。

intro.en: Marriage reaches English through Old French mariage from Latin maritare 'to wed', a verb built on maritus 'husband'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: marriage 经古法语 mariage 来自拉丁 maritare「使成婚」，该动词由 maritus「丈夫」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Maritus meant 'husband, married man', with the feminine marita 'wife'. Its deeper origin is uncertain: the link to mas 'male' is often proposed but not demonstrated.
items.cn: maritus 意为「丈夫、已婚男子」，阴性形式为 marita「妻子」。其更深来源不确定：把它与 mas「男性」联系起来是常见假说，但未获证实。

items.en: Maritare meant 'to wed, to give in marriage', and was also used of joining a vine to a supporting tree, an image of two lives bound together.
items.cn: maritare 意为「使成婚、嫁娶」，也用于把葡萄藤接到支撑的树上，暗含两条生命被绑在一起。

items.en: Old French mariage named both the wedded state and the wedding feast, and carried both senses into English in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 mariage 同时指已婚状态与婚宴，并在十三世纪把这两个义项带入英语。

items.en: English marriage kept the double sense from the start, so the same word names the relation and the day that begins it.
items.cn: 英语 marriage 从一开始就保留双重含义，同一个词既指关系，也指开启关系的那一天。

items.en: Canon law made marriage one of the sacraments, while civil law made it a contract with property consequences; both uses shaped the modern word.
items.cn: 教会法把婚姻列为圣事之一，世俗法则把它变成带有财产后果的契约；两种用法共同塑造了现代词义。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): no convincing Latin derivation of maritus has been established, and the recorded first uses of the card-game sense are not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：maritus 尚无令人信服的拉丁派生来源；纸牌游戏义的最早书证年代也不固定。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin stock; group two holds near synonyms for the union or the event.
note.cn: 第一组是同出这一拉丁词干的词；第二组是表示结合或仪式的近义词。

entries.definition: To take as a spouse or to join two people as spouses; marriage is the resulting state or event.
entries.definitionCN: 指娶、嫁或为两人证婚；marriage 是由此形成的状态或事件。

entries.definition: Of or relating to marriage, used in legal and medical contexts rather than in everyday talk.
entries.definitionCN: 指与婚姻有关的形容词，多用于法律与医学语境，而非日常口语。

entries.definition: A formal or religious word for the married state, felt as more solemn than marriage.
entries.definitionCN: 指已婚状态正式或宗教性的说法，比 marriage 更显庄重。

entries.definition: An old borrowing of the same French word, later displaced by marriage; it survives only in historical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 同一法语词的古老借形，后来被 marriage 取代，只在历史文献中留存。

entries.definition: The ceremony and its celebration, without saying anything about the years that follow.
entries.definitionCN: 只指仪式及其庆祝，不涉及婚后的岁月。

entries.definition: A general word for two things becoming one, used of states, trade bodies and couples alike.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指两物合而为一，国家、工会与伴侣都可使用。

entries.definition: A formal, often journalistic word for a wedding, always plural and slightly ornamental.
entries.definitionCN: 指婚礼的正式用语，常见于报道，总是复数且略带修饰色彩。

entries.definition: A lasting arrangement between two people or firms; it makes no claim about vows or law.
entries.definitionCN: 指两人或两家公司之间的长期安排，不涉及誓言或法律。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: maritus meant husband, and -age turns the person into the state: the husband-state, then the union.
normal.cn: maritus 指丈夫，-age 把人变成状态：先是「丈夫的身份」，再是婚姻。

normal.en: The family runs marry, marriage, marital, premarital, extramarital and marriageable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 marry、marriage、marital、premarital、extramarital 与 marriageable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: arranged marriage, marriage vows, marriage license, marriage of convenience.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：包办婚姻、结婚誓言、结婚证书、权宜婚姻。

normal.en: The metaphor is alive in phrases like a marriage of flavours or a marriage of styles.
normal.cn: 比喻义仍活跃，如风味的结合、风格的结合。

normal.en: The card game sense survives in regional play and in dictionaries, not in general speech.
normal.cn: 纸牌义仍留在地方玩法与词典中，日常口语已不常用。

abstract.en: Picture two streams meeting and then sharing one bed.
abstract.cn: 想象两条溪流汇合后共用一条河床。

abstract.en: Picture a knot tied in public and carried privately for years.
abstract.cn: 想象一个当众打好的结，被私人携带多年。

abstract.en: Picture a vine grafted onto a tree so that both keep growing.
abstract.cn: 想象一根藤接到树上，两者都继续生长。

examples.en: The law recognizes a marriage only after both parties sign the register.
examples.cn: 法律只有在双方签署登记簿后才承认婚姻。

examples.en: Their marriage survived drought, debt and two long separations.
examples.cn: 他们的婚姻熬过了干旱、债务与两次长期分离。

examples.en: Critics called the novel a marriage of detective plot and family saga.
examples.cn: 评论家称这部小说是侦探情节与家族史诗的结合。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「marry（结婚）+ age（年龄）」——到了年纪就结婚

root: 拉丁 maritus「丈夫」（阴性 marita「妻子」）→ 动词 maritare「使成婚」→ 古法语 mariage → 英语 marriage。maritus 的更深来源不确定，与 mas「男性」的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one bond: two people are joined, and the joining is then read as an event, a daily state, a social rule, a metaphor, a game, a sacrament, a treaty and a register entry.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个结合展开：两个人被连在一起，这个结合再依次被读作事件、日常状态、社会制度、比喻、游戏、圣事、盟约与登记记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rings set side by side on one sheet of paper, neither complete without the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两枚戒指并排放在同一张纸上，缺一枚都不成双。

branches.en: THE BOND AND ITS RECORD: the relation comes first, and the register is how a state sees it.
branches.cn: 结合与记录：关系在先，登记则是国家看见它的方式。

branches.en: THE DAY AND THE VOW: a public rite turns a private promise into a recognised union.
branches.cn: 那一天与那誓言：公开仪式把私下承诺变成被承认的结合。

branches.en: THE LONG MIDDLE: most of a marriage is neither the wedding nor the law but ordinary duration.
branches.cn: 漫长的中间段：婚姻的大部分既不是婚礼也不是法律，而是平常的持续。

branches.en: RULES AND ALLIANCES: a group can define the form, and families can use it as a treaty.
branches.cn: 规则与联盟：群体可以规定形式，家族也可以把它当作条约。

branches.en: TWO BECOME ONE: the metaphor and the card game both play on the matched pair.
branches.cn: 合二为一：比喻义与纸牌义都借成对之物做文章。

intro.en: Marriage is a Latin noun stem plus a French ending, and the same stem builds the legal, medical and everyday words around it.
intro.cn: marriage 由一个拉丁名词词干加一个法语词尾构成，同一词干还构成它周围的法律、医学与日常用词。

latinIntro.en: Latin maritus and marita sit behind marriage, marry and marital; the ending -age names a state or a collection.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 maritus 与 marita 是 marriage、marry 与 marital 的来源；词尾 -age 表状态或集合。

items.example: Maritus supplied the whole family of words.
items.exampleCN: maritus 提供了整个词族的来源。

items.example: The feminine form fills out the pair.
items.exampleCN: 阴性形式补全了这一对。

items.structure: maritare, maritavi, maritatum (Latin verb, first conjugation)
items.example: The verb could also mean to join a vine to a tree.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词也可指把藤接到树上。

items.example: The suffix turns the act of wedding into a lasting state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把成婚之举变成持续状态。

items.example: Old French kept both senses in one word.
items.exampleCN: 古法语用一个词保留了这两个义项。

items.example: English kept the double sense intact.
items.exampleCN: 英语完整保留了这双重含义。

items.example: Marry is the verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: marry 是名词背后的动词。

items.meaning: relating to a husband or to marriage
items.example: Marital law speaks of duties between spouses.
items.exampleCN: 婚姻法讲的是配偶之间的义务。

items.example: Premarital agreements are signed before the wedding.
items.exampleCN: 婚前协议在婚礼之前签署。

items.example: Extramarital adds the idea of crossing a boundary.
items.exampleCN: extramarital 增添了越界的意思。

definition_zh: 与婚姻有关的；夫妻之间的
definition_en: relating to marriage or to the relationship between spouses
core_image: 一份表格上「配偶」一栏被红笔圈起，旁边压着两张并排的身份证
scene: 诊室的桌上摊着一份表格，婚姻状况那一栏被反复圈画。The clinic asks every patient about marital status before treatment.
sceneCN: 这里 marital 指「与婚姻有关的」（第 1 个义项：涉及婚姻这一制度或状态）；句意为诊所在治疗前会询问每位病人的婚姻状况。可辨识物件：表格、红笔、身份证、诊室桌。

senses.title: Relating to the institution of marriage
senses.definition: connected with marriage as a social and legal institution rather than with a particular couple
senses.definitionCN: 指与作为社会与法律制度的婚姻相关，而非与某一对夫妻相关
senses.example: The clinic asks every patient about marital status before treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所在治疗前会询问每位病人的婚姻状况。
senses.why: the adjective was built from maritus 'husband', so it points at the institution a husband enters.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词由 maritus「丈夫」构成，指向丈夫所进入的那项制度。

senses.title: Between the spouses themselves
senses.definition: describing what passes between two married people, such as trust, duty or silence
senses.definitionCN: 描述两个已婚者之间流动的东西，如信任、义务或沉默
senses.example: Their marital arguments were never discussed outside the house.
senses.exampleCN: 他们夫妻间的争吵从不对外人提起。
senses.why: the same adjective narrows from the institution to the two people inside it.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词从制度收窄到制度之内的两个人。

senses.title: Legal status of being married
senses.definition: the official classification of a person as married, single, divorced or widowed
senses.definitionCN: 把一个人正式归为已婚、未婚、离异或丧偶的分类
senses.example: Applicants must state their marital status on the form.
senses.exampleCN: 申请人必须在表格上写明婚姻状况。
senses.why: states need a recorded category, so marital became the standard label for it.
senses.whyCN: 国家需要一个登记类别，marital 就成了这个类别的标准标签。

senses.title: Property and rights inside marriage
senses.definition: belonging to the household or the rights that spouses hold in law
senses.definitionCN: 指属于婚内家庭或配偶依法享有的权利
senses.example: The marital home is usually treated separately in a divorce.
senses.exampleCN: 离婚时，婚居住所通常单独处理。
senses.why: property is where the abstract institution becomes a set of enforceable claims.
senses.whyCN: 财产正是抽象制度变成可执行主张的地方。

senses.title: Quality and adjustment of the relationship
senses.definition: used by researchers for satisfaction, stress and adjustment between partners
senses.definitionCN: 研究者用来指伴侣之间的满意度、压力与调适
senses.example: The study measured marital satisfaction twice a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究每年两次测量婚姻满意度。
senses.why: social science needed a neutral adjective that could modify satisfaction and stress.
senses.whyCN: 社会科学需要一个中性形容词来修饰满意度与压力。

senses.title: Conflict and violence within marriage
senses.definition: describing quarrels, abuse or separation that occur between spouses
senses.definitionCN: 描述配偶之间发生的争吵、虐待或分居
senses.example: Marital conflict was recorded in one fifth of the households.
senses.exampleCN: 五分之一的家庭记录了婚内冲突。
senses.why: the dark side of the institution also needed a clinical label, and marital supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 制度的阴暗面也需要一个临床标签，marital 正好提供。

senses.title: Sexual relations within marriage
senses.titleCN: 婚内的性关系（学术用语）
senses.definition: a formal or clinical way of referring to intimacy between spouses
senses.definitionCN: 指配偶之间亲密关系的正式或临床说法
senses.example: Older medical texts discussed marital relations in cautious language.
senses.exampleCN: 较早的医学文献用谨慎的措辞讨论婚内性关系。
senses.why: medicine preferred an indirect adjective to the plainer words for sex.
senses.whyCN: 医学界更愿意用间接的形容词，而不用更直白的性行为词。

senses.title: Counseling and repair of the relationship
senses.definition: used of therapy, mediation and advice aimed at keeping a marriage working
senses.definitionCN: 指为维持婚姻运转而进行的治疗、调解与咨询
senses.example: They sought marital counseling before deciding to separate.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在决定分居前寻求了婚姻咨询。
senses.why: once marriage is seen as work, it also needs a repair service with a name.
senses.whyCN: 一旦婚姻被视为一项工作，它也就需要有名有姓的维修服务。

intro.en: Marital comes from Latin maritalis 'of a husband, of marriage', an adjective built on maritus 'husband'. It entered English in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: marital 来自拉丁 maritalis「丈夫的、婚姻的」，该形容词由 maritus「丈夫」构成，十六世纪进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Maritus meant 'husband, married man'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the connection sometimes proposed with mas 'male' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: maritus 意为「丈夫、已婚男子」。其更深来源不确定；有人提出它与 mas「男性」有关，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: The suffix -alis formed relational adjectives, so maritalis meant 'belonging to a husband or to marriage' rather than 'warlike' or 'masculine'.
items.cn: 后缀 -alis 构成关系形容词，因此 maritalis 意为「属于丈夫或婚姻的」，而非「好战的」或「男性化的」。

items.en: English took the adjective directly from Latin in the sixteenth century, at first in legal and theological writing about the duties of spouses.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪直接从拉丁语借入这个形容词，最初用于讨论配偶义务的法律与神学写作。

items.en: Registration forms and medical texts made marital a fixed label for status, property and intimacy.
items.cn: 登记表格与医学文献使 marital 成为身份、财产与亲密关系的固定标签。

items.en: Twentieth-century psychology and sociology extended it to satisfaction, stress, conflict and counseling.
items.cn: 二十世纪的心理学与社会学把它扩展到满意度、压力、冲突与咨询。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin history of maritus is not settled, and the earliest uses of the counseling sense are dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：maritus 在拉丁语之前的历史尚无定论，咨询义的最早用法也只有约略年代。

note.en: Group one holds forms that look alike and are constantly confused, including one that comes from a different root entirely; group two holds near synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组是形近且常被混淆的形式，其中有一个来自完全不同的词源；第二组是近义词。

entries.definition: Means 'warlike, of soldiers', from Mars, the Roman god of war; it has no connection with marriage.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「战争的、军事的」，来自罗马战神 Mars，与婚姻毫无关系。

entries.definition: The institution or the wedding; marital is the adjective that describes it.
entries.definitionCN: 指婚姻制度或婚礼；marital 是描述它的形容词。

entries.definition: Says that a person has a spouse; marital says that something belongs to marriage.
entries.definitionCN: 指某人已有配偶；marital 指某事物属于婚姻。

entries.definition: The act of taking a spouse or joining two people; the adjective never carries the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指娶、嫁或为两人证婚的行为；形容词不表动作。

entries.definition: From Latin coniugium 'yoke, marriage', stressing the bond between the two partners.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 coniugium「轭、婚姻」，强调两个伴侣之间的结合。

entries.definition: A formal synonym tied to matrimony, common in property and court language.
entries.definitionCN: 与 matrimony 相关的正式同义词，常见于财产与法庭用语。

entries.definition: Relating to a spouse as a person, as in spousal support; it names the person, not the institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指与配偶个人有关，如配偶赡养；它指人，而非制度。

entries.definition: Means married, and by extension stubbornly attached to an idea, as in wedded to a method.
entries.definitionCN: 意为已婚的，引申为固执于某种想法，如固守一种方法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: maritus 'husband' plus -alis 'belonging to' gives 'belonging to a husband', then 'belonging to marriage'.
normal.cn: maritus「丈夫」加 -alis「属于……的」，先得「属于丈夫的」，再得「属于婚姻的」。

normal.en: Do not confuse marital with martial: one is marriage, the other is Mars.
normal.cn: 不要把 marital 与 martial 混淆：一个关乎婚姻，一个关乎战神。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: marital status, marital home, marital breakdown, marital counseling.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：婚姻状况、婚居住所、婚姻破裂、婚姻咨询。

normal.en: The family runs marriage, married, marry, premarital, extramarital and nonmarital.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 marriage、married、marry、premarital、extramarital 与 nonmarital。

normal.en: Administrative forms made the word familiar long before anyone studied marriage.
normal.cn: 在有人研究婚姻之前，行政表格就已让这个词变得常见。

abstract.en: Picture a box on a form that decides which legal doors open.
abstract.cn: 想象表格上的一个方框，它决定哪些法律之门会打开。

abstract.en: Picture two signatures sharing one margin.
abstract.cn: 想象两个签名共用一个页边。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge inspected not for its view but for its weight-bearing joints.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥，人们检查的不是风景，而是承重的接缝。

examples.en: Hospital records usually note marital status at admission.
examples.cn: 医院记录通常在入院时注明婚姻状况。

examples.en: The survey linked marital stress to long working hours.
examples.cn: 这项调查把婚姻压力与长时间工作联系起来。

examples.en: They signed a marital agreement before buying the flat together.
examples.cn: 他们在共同买房前签署了一份婚姻协议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「marry（结婚）+ tal（形容词尾）」——跟婚姻有关的；注意别和 martial（军事的）混

root: 拉丁 maritus「丈夫」加 -alis「属于……的」构成 maritalis，十六世纪进入英语。maritus 的更深来源不确定，与 mas「男性」的联系仅为假说；martial 来自战神 Mars，二者无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one label: something belongs to marriage, and the label is then attached to a status, a household, a quality, a conflict, an intimacy and a repair service.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个标签展开：某事物属于婚姻，这个标签再依次贴到身份、家庭、质量、冲突、亲密关系与修复服务上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one box on a form, circled in red, that decides which doors open.
core.cn: 核心意象：表格上一个被红笔圈起的方框，它决定哪些门会打开。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION: the adjective begins as a general pointer to marriage itself.
branches.cn: 制度：这个形容词起初只是泛指婚姻本身。

branches.en: THE COUPLE: the same pointer turns inward toward what passes between two people.
branches.cn: 夫妻：同一个指向转向内部，指向两个人之间流动的东西。

branches.en: THE RECORD AND THE ASSETS: a state writes the status down, and property follows the entry.
branches.cn: 记录与资产：国家把身份写下，财产则随这条记录而来。

branches.en: THE MEASURABLE MIDDLE: satisfaction and stress can be scored like any other variable.
branches.cn: 可测量的中间段：满意度与压力可以像其他变量一样打分。

branches.en: DARK SIDE AND REPAIR: conflict and intimacy are named clinically, and both lead to counseling.
branches.cn: 暗面与修复：冲突与亲密关系都被临床化命名，二者都通向咨询。

intro.en: Marital is a Latin relational adjective: a noun stem plus a suffix that means 'belonging to', with English prefixes later building the before-marriage and outside-marriage variants.
intro.cn: marital 是拉丁关系形容词：名词词干加一个意为「属于……」的后缀，后来的英语前缀又构成婚前与婚外等变体。

latinIntro.en: Latin maritus supplied the stem and -alis supplied the relational ending; the same pair builds maritalis and, through French, marriage.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 maritus 提供词干，-alis 提供关系形容词词尾；同一组合构成 maritalis，并经法语构成 marriage。

items.example: The stem names the person who enters the state.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干指进入该状态的人。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into a relational adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成关系形容词。

items.example: Maritalis covered both the person and the institution.
items.exampleCN: maritalis 同时涵盖人与制度。

items.example: English kept the Latin shape almost unchanged.
items.exampleCN: 英语几乎原样保留了拉丁词形。

items.example: Maritally, the two households remained separate.
items.exampleCN: 在婚姻关系上，这两户人家仍各自独立。

items.example: Premarital testing became common in the twentieth century.
items.exampleCN: 婚前检查在二十世纪变得普遍。

items.example: The prefix marks a boundary crossed.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记一条被越过的界线。

items.example: Nonmarital births are counted separately.
items.exampleCN: 非婚生育单独统计。

items.example: The noun names what the adjective describes.
items.exampleCN: 名词指形容词所描述的事物。

items.example: Married describes the person, not the institution.
items.exampleCN: married 描述人，而非制度。

latinEntries.meaning: of a husband or of marriage

definition_zh: 围绕订婚、婚礼与婚后生活形成的传统做法与规矩
definition_en: the traditional practices and rules that surround engagement, wedding ceremonies and the start of married life
core_image: 喜堂门口摆着两双新鞋，桌上一盘红枣与花生，来客按辈分依次拱手
scene: 喜堂的门口摆着两双新鞋，桌上放着一盘红枣和花生，来客按辈分依次行礼。Village marriage customs require the bride to circle the fire three times.
sceneCN: 这里 marriage customs 指「围绕婚事形成的传统做法与规矩」（第 1 个义项：一整套在婚礼前后被遵循的习俗）；句意为村里的婚姻习俗要求新娘绕火三圈。可辨识物件：新鞋、红枣、花生、喜堂、火盆。

pos.zh: 婚姻习俗（复数名词短语）

senses.title: Traditional practices around a wedding
senses.titleCN: 婚礼前后遵循的传统做法
senses.definition: the expected actions and taboos that a community follows when a couple marry
senses.definitionCN: 一个社群在两人成婚时所遵循的既定行为与禁忌
senses.example: Village marriage customs require the bride to circle the fire three times.
senses.exampleCN: 村里的婚姻习俗要求新娘绕火三圈。
senses.why: custom is habitual practice, and marriage is the occasion where practice is most tightly scripted.
senses.whyCN: custom 指习惯性做法，而婚姻正是这种做法被规定得最细的场合。

senses.title: Practices of betrothal
senses.definition: the steps of proposing, negotiating and formally promising a future marriage
senses.definitionCN: 提亲、商谈并正式许诺未来婚事的各个步骤
senses.example: Betrothal customs in that region begin with a gift of tea.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的订婚习俗以送茶开始。
senses.why: the wedding is the visible end, so most of the customs begin earlier and quietly.
senses.whyCN: 婚礼是看得见的终点，因此许多习俗更早、更安静地开始。

senses.title: Exchange of bride price and dowry
senses.definition: the transfer of goods or money between the families of the bride and groom
senses.definitionCN: 新娘与新郞两家之间转移财物或金钱
senses.example: Marriage customs once fixed the amount of the bride price.
senses.exampleCN: 婚姻习俗曾规定聘礼的数额。
senses.why: a marriage joins two households as well as two people, and goods mark that join.
senses.whyCN: 婚姻既连接两个人，也连接两户人家，财物正是这一连接的标记。

senses.title: Symbolic acts in the ceremony
senses.titleCN: 婚礼仪式中的象征行为
senses.definition: gestures such as exchanging rings, veiling the bride or circling a fire that carry meaning beyond the literal act
senses.definitionCN: 交换戒指、为新娘盖头、绕火等带有字面之外含义的动作
senses.example: The rings are only one of many symbolic marriage customs.
senses.exampleCN: 戒指只是众多象征性婚姻习俗之一。
senses.why: customs work by symbol: a small act stands for a large promise.
senses.whyCN: 习俗靠象征运作：一个小动作代表一个大承诺。

senses.title: Rules about where the couple lives
senses.definition: the expectation that a new couple lives with the groom's or the bride's family
senses.definitionCN: 新婚夫妇随夫家或随妻家居住的期待
senses.example: Marriage customs in the valley favour living near the husband's parents.
senses.exampleCN: 山谷里的婚姻习俗偏向住在丈夫父母附近。
senses.why: residence decides which household gains a worker, so it is a rule, not a detail.
senses.whyCN: 居住地决定哪一户多得一个劳动力，因此它是规则而非细节。

senses.title: Marriage taboos and prohibitions
senses.titleCN: 与婚姻相关的禁忌与禁例
senses.definition: rules forbidding certain partners, dates or actions as dangerous or impure
senses.definitionCN: 因危险或不洁而禁止某些配偶、日期或行为的规则
senses.example: Customs forbade marriage between people sharing a surname.
senses.exampleCN: 习俗禁止同姓者通婚。
senses.why: every custom has a fence, and marriage customs fence off who may marry whom.
senses.whyCN: 每种习俗都有围栏，而婚姻习俗围住的是谁可以与谁成婚。

senses.title: Comparison across cultures
senses.titleCN: 不同文化婚姻习俗的比较
senses.definition: the scholarly description and comparison of wedding practices in different societies
senses.definitionCN: 对不同社会中婚礼做法的学术描述与比较
senses.example: The course compares marriage customs from six regions.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程比较六个地区的婚姻习俗。
senses.why: once practices are written down, they become objects that can be set side by side.
senses.whyCN: 做法一旦被记录下来，就成了可以并排放置的对象。

senses.title: Simplification and revival today
senses.titleCN: 当代的简化与传统习俗的复兴
senses.definition: the modern trimming of elaborate rites and the deliberate return to older forms
senses.definitionCN: 现代对繁复礼仪的删减，以及有意回归旧形式
senses.example: Young couples now mix civil marriage customs with a traditional tea rite.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻夫妻如今把民事婚姻习俗与传统敬茶礼混在一起。
senses.why: customs survive by being edited, not by being frozen.
senses.whyCN: 习俗靠被改写而存活，而非靠被冻结。

intro.en: Marriage customs joins marriage, from Latin maritus 'husband' through Old French, with custom, from Latin consuetudo 'habit, usage' through Old French costume. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: marriage customs 由 marriage 与 custom 合成：marriage 经古法语来自拉丁 maritus「丈夫」，custom 经古法语 costume 来自拉丁 consuetudo「习惯、惯例」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Maritus meant 'husband', and maritare 'to wed' produced Old French mariage and English marriage. The deeper origin of maritus is uncertain, and the link to mas 'male' is only a hypothesis.
items.cn: maritus 意为「丈夫」，动词 maritare「使成婚」衍生出古法语 mariage 与英语 marriage。maritus 的更深来源不确定，与 mas「男性」的联系仅是假说。

items.en: Consuetudo meant 'habit, custom, usage', built on consuescere 'to accustom', itself con- 'thoroughly' plus suescere 'to become used'.
items.cn: consuetudo 意为「习惯、风俗、惯例」，由 consuescere「使习惯」构成，而后者是 con-「彻底」加 suescere「变得习惯」。

items.en: Old French costume carried both 'habit' and 'usual practice' into English, where custom kept the social sense.
items.cn: 古法语 costume 把「习惯」与「惯常做法」带入英语，custom 保留了社会性含义。

items.en: English joined the two nouns to name the rules that surround a wedding, usually in the plural because a wedding is a sequence of acts.
items.cn: 英语把这两个名词组合起来，指围绕婚礼的规矩；因婚礼是一连串动作，通常用复数。

items.en: Comparative anthropology made marriage customs a standard category for describing how societies arrange unions.
items.cn: 比较人类学使 marriage customs 成为描述各社会如何安排婚姻的标准类别。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the plural phrase is recorded only from modern field reports, and no single first use is fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个复数短语只见于近代田野报告，没有确切的最早书证。

note.en: Group one holds words built from the same two stems; group two holds terms for rules and rites that are often confused with custom.
note.cn: 第一组是同出这两个词干的词；第二组是常与 custom 混淆的规则与仪式类词。

entries.definition: A habitual practice of a group; marriage customs are the practices attached to one occasion.
entries.definitionCN: 指群体的习惯性做法；婚姻习俗则是附着于某一场合的做法。

entries.definition: Means 'according to custom'; it describes a practice, while the noun names it.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「按习俗的」；它描述做法，名词则指做法本身。

entries.definition: From the same Old French word in the sense of habitual use: one who comes habitually to a shop.
entries.definitionCN: 来自同一古法语词的「惯常使用」义：习惯性来店里的人。

entries.definition: The same Old French word that gave custom, now meaning dress; the two meanings split in English.
entries.definitionCN: 与 custom 同出一个古法语词，今指服装；两个含义在英语中分化。

entries.definition: A prescribed religious or solemn act; customs may include rites but are broader and less formal.
entries.definitionCN: 指规定的宗教或庄严行为；习俗可包含仪式，但范围更广、更不正式。

entries.definition: Anything passed from generation to generation; custom stresses repeated practice rather than age alone.
entries.definitionCN: 指代代相传的一切；custom 强调反复实践，而不只是年代久远。

entries.definition: A rule accepted by agreement, often recent; custom is older and unwritten.
entries.definitionCN: 指经同意而被接受的规则，往往较新；custom 更古老且不成文。

entries.definition: A rule enforced by a state; a custom may be written into law, but it begins without that force.
entries.definitionCN: 指由国家强制执行的规则；习俗可被写入法律，但它起初并无这种强制力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: marriage comes from maritus 'husband'; custom comes from consuetudo 'habit'.
normal.cn: marriage 来自 maritus「丈夫」；custom 来自 consuetudo「习惯」。

normal.en: The plural is normal because a wedding is a chain of small acts, not one act.
normal.cn: 用复数很正常，因为婚礼是一连串小动作，而非单个动作。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: local marriage customs, traditional marriage customs, observe marriage customs.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：地方婚姻习俗、传统婚姻习俗、遵守婚姻习俗。

normal.en: The family runs custom, customary, customer and customize, though their meanings have drifted apart.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 custom、customary、customer 与 customize，但词义已经分化。

normal.en: Anthropology treats the phrase as a category for comparison, not as advice for couples.
normal.cn: 人类学把这个短语当作比较类别，而非给新人的建议。

abstract.en: Picture a script passed down for a wedding nobody remembers writing.
abstract.cn: 想象一场婚礼的脚本代代相传，却没人记得是谁写的。

abstract.en: Picture two families exchanging goods as a sentence exchanges subjects.
abstract.cn: 想象两户人家交换财物，就像句子交换主语。

abstract.en: Picture a fence built from habits rather than from wood.
abstract.cn: 想象一道用习惯而非木头筑成的围栏。

examples.en: The museum collected photographs of marriage customs from fifty villages.
examples.cn: 博物馆收集了五十个村庄的婚姻习俗照片。

examples.en: Migration changed marriage customs faster than law did.
examples.cn: 迁徙改变婚姻习俗的速度快于法律。

examples.en: Some marriage customs survive mainly as performance for visitors.
examples.cn: 有些婚姻习俗如今主要作为给游客看的表演而存在。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「marriage（婚姻）+ customs（习俗）」——办喜事时一套套的老规矩

root: marriage 来自拉丁 maritus「丈夫」经古法语 mariage；custom 来自拉丁 consuetudo「习惯、惯例」经古法语 costume。maritus 的更深来源不确定，与 mas「男性」的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one script: a community writes down how a marriage should be made, and that script covers betrothal, goods, symbols, residence, taboos, comparison and modern revision.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一套脚本展开：一个社群写下婚事应当如何办，这套脚本涵盖订婚、财物、象征、居住、禁忌、比较与现代改写。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wedding script written in gestures rather than words, performed in the same order each time.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份用动作而非文字写成的婚礼脚本，每次按同样顺序演出。

branches.en: THE WHOLE SCRIPT: the phrase names the full set of expected actions before any single one.
branches.cn: 整套脚本：这个短语先指全部被期待的动作，再指其中任何一项。

branches.en: BEFORE AND ACROSS: betrothal is the quiet opening, and comparison turns the script into an object of study.
branches.cn: 之前与横比：订婚是安静的开端，比较则把脚本变成研究对象。

branches.en: GOODS THAT BIND: the transfer of wealth is a sentence spoken in objects.
branches.cn: 以物相系：财物的转移是用物件说出的句子。

branches.en: SIGNS AND FENCES: symbolic acts say what is promised, and taboos say what is forbidden.
branches.cn: 符号与围栏：象征动作说出承诺，禁忌说出禁止。

branches.en: WHERE AND WHETHER: residence decides who gains a worker, and revival decides which parts still speak.
branches.cn: 住在哪与是否延续：居住决定谁多得劳力，复兴决定哪些部分仍有话说。

intro.en: The phrase combines a Latin-derived noun of marriage with a Latin-derived noun of habit, and both stems carry their own suffixes into English.
intro.cn: 这个短语把一个源自拉丁的婚姻名词与一个源自拉丁的习惯名词组合起来，两个词干都带着各自的后缀进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Latin maritus and consuetudo stand behind the two halves; -age turns the wedding act into a state, while the custom family loses its Latin ending in French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 maritus 与 consuetudo 分别是两半的来源；-age 把成婚之举变成状态，而 custom 一族在法语中丢掉了拉丁词尾。

items.example: The first half of the phrase begins with the husband.
items.exampleCN: 短语的前一半从丈夫说起。

items.example: The verb supplied the French noun of marriage.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供了法语的婚姻名词。

items.example: The suffix makes a state out of an act.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把行为变成状态。

items.example: Marriage names what the customs surround.
items.exampleCN: marriage 指习俗所围绕的那件事。

items.example: Consuetudo is the source of the second half.
items.exampleCN: consuetudo 是短语后一半的来源。

items.example: A custom is what a group has grown used to.
items.exampleCN: 习俗就是一个群体逐渐习惯的东西。

items.example: Old French costume meant practice before it meant dress.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 costume 先指做法，后指服装。

items.example: Custom kept the social sense and lost the clothing sense.
items.exampleCN: custom 保留了社会义，丢掉了服装义。

items.example: Customary acts are the ones the phrase collects.
items.exampleCN: 按习俗的行为正是这个短语所汇集的对象。

items.structure: custom + -er, from the sense of habitual use
items.example: A customer was once simply a person wont to come.
items.exampleCN: 顾客原只是习惯于常来的人。

definition_zh: 按固定程序进行的一套仪式；也指仪式性的
definition_en: a set of actions performed in a fixed order, especially for religious or solemn purposes, and the adjective describing such actions
core_image: 清晨的神龛前摆好米碗与清水，最年长的人先点上一炷香，其余人依次跟上
scene: 清晨的神龛前摆好米碗与清水，家里最年长的人先点上一炷香。The opening ritual of the festival begins at dawn with a single bell.
sceneCN: 这里 ritual 指「按固定程序进行的一套仪式」（第 1 个义项：有既定顺序的庄严动作）；句意为节日的开场仪式在黎明时以一声钟响开始。可辨识物件：神龛、米碗、清水、香、钟。

senses.title: A set of actions in fixed order
senses.titleCN: 按固定顺序进行的一套动作
senses.definition: a sequence of actions repeated in the same order on the same kind of occasion
senses.definitionCN: 在同类场合按同样顺序重复的一连串动作
senses.example: The opening ritual of the festival begins at dawn with a single bell.
senses.exampleCN: 节日的开场仪式在黎明时以一声钟响开始。
senses.why: ritus named a religious rite, and the noun keeps the idea of an order that must not be varied.
senses.whyCN: ritus 指宗教仪式，这个名词保留了「顺序不可更改」的意思。

senses.title: The ordered rites of worship
senses.definition: the prescribed words and gestures of a religious service
senses.definitionCN: 宗教礼拜中规定的言辞与动作
senses.example: The priest followed the ritual exactly, down to the last bow.
senses.exampleCN: 司仪严格遵循仪式，连最后一次鞠躬也不差。
senses.why: religion is where fixed order is felt to be most necessary, so the word grew strong there.
senses.whyCN: 宗教最能感到固定顺序的必要，这个词也在此处扎根最深。

senses.title: A personal daily routine
senses.definition: a small repeated sequence that marks a part of the day, such as coffee before work
senses.definitionCN: 标记一天中某段时间的重复小序列，如上班前的咖啡
senses.example: Her morning ritual is a cup of tea and ten minutes of silence.
senses.exampleCN: 她的晨间固定程序是一杯茶和十分钟的安静。
senses.why: the word moved from the altar to the kitchen because both need a dependable order.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从祭坛移到厨房，因为两者都需要可靠的顺序。

senses.title: Stylized social courtesy
senses.titleCN: 社会交往中的程式化礼节
senses.definition: the expected words and gestures of greeting, toasting or taking leave
senses.definitionCN: 问候、敬酒或告别时所期待的言辞与动作
senses.example: Their greeting was a ritual of three bows and two questions.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的问候是一套三鞠躬加两个问题的礼节。
senses.why: social life repeats its own small liturgies, and the same noun covers them.
senses.whyCN: 社会生活重复着自己的小礼序，同一个名词也就涵盖了它们。

senses.title: Rites marking a change of status
senses.titleCN: 标记身份转变的过渡仪式
senses.definition: ceremonies such as birth rites, initiation or funerals that move a person from one state to another
senses.definitionCN: 出生礼、成年礼或葬礼等把人从一种状态转入另一种状态的仪式
senses.example: The initiation ritual lasted three days and ended with a new name.
senses.exampleCN: 成年仪式持续三天，最后以一个新名字结束。
senses.why: anthropology found that the most important rituals mark a crossing, not a repetition.
senses.whyCN: 人类学发现最重要的仪式标记的是跨越，而非重复。

senses.title: Repetition that has become compulsive
senses.titleCN: 仪式化的重复行为（心理层面）
senses.definition: a repeated act that calms anxiety or must be performed to avoid distress
senses.definitionCN: 为安抚焦虑而重复、或必须执行以避免痛苦的动作
senses.example: He developed a private ritual of checking the lock four times.
senses.exampleCN: 他养成了一个私下的仪式：把锁检查四次。
senses.why: psychology borrowed the word because compulsion has the same outward shape as rite.
senses.whyCN: 心理学借用这个词，因为强迫行为与仪式在外形上相同。

senses.title: Symbolic acts that bind a group
senses.definition: public gestures such as flag-raising or oath-taking that make a group feel itself
senses.definitionCN: 升旗或宣誓等让群体感到自身存在的公开动作
senses.example: The school's Monday ritual assembled every class on the field.
senses.exampleCN: 学校周一的仪式把每个班都召集到操场上。
senses.why: a group needs a body, and repeated gestures give it one.
senses.whyCN: 群体需要一个形体，而重复的动作提供了这个形体。

senses.title: Ritual as an adjective
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean 'of, or used in, a rite'
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，表示「仪式的」或「仪式中使用的」
senses.example: The ritual dance is performed only by the elders.
senses.exampleCN: 这种仪式之舞只由长者表演。
senses.why: the adjective is simply the noun doing modifying work, a common English shift.
senses.whyCN: 形容词只是名词在起修饰作用，这是英语常见的转用。

senses.title: A fixed routine that feels obligatory
senses.titleCN: 例行公事般的固定做法
senses.definition: a practice repeated so often that it has lost its original purpose
senses.definitionCN: 重复得太频繁、已失去原初目的的做法
senses.example: The weekly meeting had become a ritual nobody questioned.
senses.exampleCN: 每周例会已成了一套无人质疑的例行程序。
senses.why: when order outlives meaning, the word turns slightly ironic.
senses.whyCN: 当顺序比意义活得更久，这个词就带上了一点讽刺。

intro.en: Ritual comes from Latin ritualis 'relating to rites', from ritus 'a rite, a religious ceremony', through Old French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ritual 经古法语来自拉丁 ritualis「与仪式有关的」，而 ritualis 出自 ritus「仪式、宗教典礼」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ritus meant 'a rite, a religious ceremony, a custom'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the link sometimes suggested to a Vedic word for fixed order is a hypothesis, not an established derivation.
items.cn: ritus 意为「仪式、宗教典礼、惯例」。其更深来源不确定；有人把它与吠陀语中表示「固定秩序」的词相联系，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: The suffix -alis made a relational adjective, so ritualis meant 'belonging to a rite' and covered both books and gestures.
items.cn: 后缀 -alis 构成关系形容词，因此 ritualis 意为「属于仪式的」，书籍与动作都可用它形容。

items.en: Old French carried the adjective and noun into English, where ritual first named a book of church rites.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词与名词带入英语，ritual 最初指记载教会礼仪的书。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the noun meant the rites themselves, and by the nineteenth it had spread to social and personal practice.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，名词已指礼仪本身；到十九世纪，又扩展到社会与个人实践。

items.en: Both disciplines adopted the word, one for rites of passage and the other for compulsive repetition.
items.cn: 人类学与心理学都采用了这个词，前者指过渡仪式，后者指强迫性重复。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin history of ritus is unsettled, and the earliest use of the ironic 'mere routine' sense is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：ritus 在拉丁语之前的历史尚无定论，讽刺性的「只是例行公事」义的最早用法也只有约略年代。

note.en: Group one holds words built from the same stem; group two holds terms for related solemn or repeated practices.
note.cn: 第一组是同出这一词干的词；第二组是表示相关庄严或重复做法的词。

entries.definition: One prescribed ceremony, usually religious or solemn; ritual can name the whole ordered system or the style.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个规定的典礼，通常宗教或庄严；ritual 可指整套有序体系或风格。

entries.definition: Describes something done in the manner of a rite, often with a hint of excess.
entries.definitionCN: 描述以仪式方式完成的事物，常带过度拘泥的暗示。

entries.definition: Excessive attachment to rites, or the study of them as a system.
entries.definitionCN: 指对仪式的过度依附，或把仪式当作体系来研究。

entries.definition: To turn an action into a rite or to perform it in a fixed ceremonial way.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某个动作变成仪式，或以固定礼仪方式完成。

entries.definition: A formal event with a set order; it stresses occasion and dignity more than repeated practice.
entries.definitionCN: 指有固定顺序的正式活动；比「反复实践」更强调场合与庄重。

entries.definition: The prescribed form of public religious worship, usually written down for a congregation.
entries.definitionCN: 指公共宗教礼拜的规定形式，通常为会众写成文本。

entries.definition: The act of keeping a law, feast or custom; it names compliance rather than the sequence of acts.
entries.definitionCN: 指遵守法律、节期或习俗；它指遵从，而非动作序列。

entries.definition: An ordinary repeated way of doing things, without the solemn charge that ritual carries.
entries.definitionCN: 指平常重复的做事方式，不带 ritual 那种庄严意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ritus 'rite' plus -alis 'belonging to' gives 'belonging to a rite'.
normal.cn: ritus「仪式」加 -alis「属于……的」，得到「属于仪式的」。

normal.en: The family runs rite, ritual, ritualistic, ritualism, ritualize and ritualization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 rite、ritual、ritualistic、ritualism、ritualize 与 ritualization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: religious ritual, daily ritual, morning ritual, ritual dance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：宗教仪式、每日固定程序、晨间固定程序、仪式之舞。

normal.en: Anthropology links ritual to rites of passage: a crossing is marked, not merely repeated.
normal.cn: 人类学把仪式与过渡礼仪相连：被标记的是跨越，而不只是重复。

normal.en: The ironic sense appears when a routine outlives its reason, as in a meeting that is a ritual.
normal.cn: 当惯例活得比理由更久，讽刺义就出现，如「一场纯属仪式的会议」。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase whose every step must be taken in the same order.
abstract.cn: 想象一道楼梯，每一级都必须按同样顺序踏过。

abstract.en: Picture a clock that rings not to tell time but to make time feel real.
abstract.cn: 想象一座钟，它响不是为了报时，而是让时间显得真实。

abstract.en: Picture a door that only opens when three hands touch it in turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，只有三只手依次触碰才会打开。

examples.en: The harvest ritual begins with the youngest child pouring water.
examples.cn: 丰收仪式由最小的孩子倒水开始。

examples.en: Modern offices have their own rituals of greeting and leaving.
examples.cn: 现代办公室有自己的问候与告别仪式。

examples.en: The therapist asked whether the ritual reduced his anxiety.
examples.cn: 治疗师问他这套仪式是否减轻了焦虑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ri（日）+ tual」——每天按同一顺序做的事，就成了仪式

root: 拉丁 ritus「仪式、宗教典礼」→ ritualis「与仪式有关的」→ 古法语 → 英语 ritual。ritus 的更深来源不确定，与吠陀语「固定秩序」词的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one order: a sequence that must be repeated exactly, performed at an altar, in a kitchen, in a greeting, at a crossing, in a compulsion, on a flagpole and finally in an empty meeting.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个顺序展开：一套必须照样重复的动作，依次在祭坛、厨房、问候、人生关口、强迫行为、旗杆前上演，最后落到一场空洞的会议上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of bowls laid out in a fixed order, each filled only when the previous one is full.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排按固定次序摆好的碗，前一只满了才轮到下一只。

branches.en: THE ORDER ITSELF: first a sequence, then the adjective that labels anything belonging to it.
branches.cn: 顺序本身：先是动作序列，再是标记任何属于该序列之物的形容词。

branches.en: ALTAR AND CROSSING: worship repeats the order, while initiation uses it to move a person.
branches.cn: 祭坛与关口：礼拜重复顺序，成年礼则用顺序移动一个人。

branches.en: KITCHEN AND EMPTY MEETING: the same order comforts a morning and hollows out a schedule.
branches.cn: 厨房与空会：同一顺序既安抚一个早晨，也掏空一张日程。

branches.en: COURTESY AND FLAG: small greetings and public gestures both make a group hold together.
branches.cn: 礼节与旗帜：小小问候与公开动作都能让群体维系。

branches.en: COMPULSION: the shape of a rite appears without its meaning, and the repetition becomes a cage.
branches.cn: 强迫：仪式的形状还在，意义却已消失，重复变成牢笼。

intro.en: Ritual is a Latin noun stem with a relational suffix, and that stem also builds the shorter noun rite and the whole ritualistic family.
intro.cn: ritual 是一个拉丁名词词干加关系后缀，同一词干还构成较短的名词 rite 与整个 ritualistic 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ritus supplied the stem and -alis supplied the adjective ending; English later added -istic, -ism and -ize to build manner, system and verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ritus 提供词干，-alis 提供形容词词尾；英语后来加上 -istic、-ism 与 -ize，构成方式、体系与动词。

items.example: Ritus named the ceremony before it named the style.
items.exampleCN: ritus 先指典礼，后指风格。

items.example: The suffix makes a relational adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成关系形容词。

items.example: Ritualis covered both the book and the gestures.
items.exampleCN: ritualis 同时涵盖书与动作。

items.example: The noun grew out of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 名词由形容词发展而来。

items.example: Rite is the single act; ritual is the order around it.
items.exampleCN: rite 是单个行为；ritual 是围绕它的顺序。

items.example: Ritualistic means done in the manner of a rite.
items.exampleCN: ritualistic 意为以仪式的方式完成。

items.meaning: in the manner of a rite
items.example: The adjective often hints at excess.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词常暗示过度。

items.example: Ritualism names attachment to rites.
items.exampleCN: ritualism 指对仪式的依附。

items.example: Ritualize turns an act into a rite.
items.exampleCN: ritualize 把行为变成仪式。

items.example: The room was ritually cleansed before use.
items.exampleCN: 房间在使用前按仪式洁净过。

definition_zh: 具有仪式特征的；程式化到近乎机械的
definition_en: done in the manner of a rite, especially in a fixed or exaggeratedly formal way
core_image: 后台的化妆镜前摆着一排面具，演员按固定顺序逐一戴上
scene: 后台的化妆镜前摆着一排面具，演员按固定顺序逐一戴上。The dancers moved with a ritualistic slowness that made every gesture feel ancient.
sceneCN: 这里 ritualistic 指「带有仪式特征的」（第 1 个义项：动作按仪轨般的方式完成）；句意为舞者以仪式般缓慢的动作移动，使每个手势都显得古老。可辨识物件：化妆镜、面具、戏服、幕布。

senses.title: Having the character of a rite
senses.definition: carried out with the ordered, solemn quality of a religious or formal rite
senses.definitionCN: 以宗教或正式仪式的有序、庄严方式完成
senses.example: The dancers moved with a ritualistic slowness that made every gesture feel ancient.
senses.exampleCN: 舞者以仪式般缓慢的动作移动，使每个手势都显得古老。
senses.why: ritual plus -istic means 'in the manner of a rite', so the adjective describes style rather than belief.
senses.whyCN: ritual 加 -istic 意为「以仪式的方式」，因此这个形容词描述风格而非信仰。

senses.title: Fixed to the point of being mechanical
senses.definition: repeated so exactly that the action looks automatic rather than alive
senses.definitionCN: 重复得过于精确，以致动作显得自动而非鲜活
senses.example: His ritualistic handshake never varied by a single degree.
senses.exampleCN: 他那仪式化的握手连角度都从不改变。
senses.why: a rite is fixed by definition, and the adjective turns that fixity into a criticism.
senses.whyCN: 仪式按定义就是固定的，这个形容词把这种固定变成了批评。

senses.title: Strictly following a religious order
senses.definition: observing every prescribed word and gesture of worship without deviation
senses.definitionCN: 不偏差地遵守礼拜中每一句规定言辞与动作
senses.example: The sect remained ritualistic long after the town had loosened.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上早已松弛下来，这个教派却仍严守仪轨。
senses.why: the adjective is neutral or admiring here: exactness is taken as faithfulness.
senses.whyCN: 此处形容词是中性的甚至赞许的：精确被视为虔诚。

senses.title: Compulsive repetition in psychology
senses.titleCN: 心理学中的仪式化重复行为
senses.definition: describing repeated acts performed to hold off anxiety rather than to worship
senses.definitionCN: 指为抵挡焦虑而非为敬拜而重复执行的动作
senses.example: The report described ritualistic checking that occupied two hours a day.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了一种每天占用两小时的仪式化检查。
senses.why: psychology borrowed the word because compulsion and rite share the same visible shape.
senses.whyCN: 心理学借用这个词，因为强迫行为与仪式在外形上一致。

senses.title: Stylized ritual quality in art
senses.titleCN: 艺术表演中的仪式性风格
senses.definition: describing theatre, dance or film that uses slow, formal, repeated movement
senses.definitionCN: 描述使用缓慢、正式、重复动作的戏剧、舞蹈或电影
senses.example: Critics praised the ritualistic staging of the funeral scene.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称赞葬礼一场的仪式化舞台处理。
senses.why: art borrows the authority of rites to make ordinary action feel weighty.
senses.whyCN: 艺术借仪式的权威，让寻常动作显得沉重。

senses.title: Ceremonial steps inside an organization
senses.titleCN: 组织流程中的仪式化环节
senses.definition: describing formal procedures that a group performs as much for identity as for results
senses.definitionCN: 描述群体为身份认同而非仅为结果而执行的形式化程序
senses.example: The firm's ritualistic approval chain delayed every small purchase.
senses.exampleCN: 公司仪式化的审批链让每笔小额采购都被拖延。
senses.why: organizations invent rites to make hierarchy visible, and the adjective names the cost.
senses.whyCN: 组织发明仪式以让层级可见，这个形容词则指出其代价。

senses.title: Mere going through the motions
senses.definition: done for appearance only, with the original purpose emptied out
senses.definitionCN: 只为外观而做，原初目的已被掏空
senses.example: The hearing was a ritualistic gesture with no real power.
senses.exampleCN: 那场听证只是走个仪式，并无实权。
senses.why: when form survives meaning, the word turns ironic, close to 'merely formal'.
senses.whyCN: 当形式比意义活得久，这个词就转为讽刺，近似「只是形式上」。

senses.title: Display behaviour in animal studies
senses.titleCN: 动物行为学中的仪式化展示
senses.definition: describing courtship or threat displays that are repeated in a fixed sequence
senses.definitionCN: 描述按固定序列重复的求偶或威吓展示
senses.example: Ethologists recorded the ritualistic display of the male bird.
senses.exampleCN: 动物行为学家记录了雄鸟的仪式化展示。
senses.why: animal behaviour uses the same word because fixed display serves as a signal, like a rite.
senses.whyCN: 动物行为学使用同一个词，因为固定展示像仪式一样充当信号。

intro.en: Ritualistic is English ritual plus the suffix -istic, which came through Latin from Greek -istikos 'in the manner of'. Ritual itself comes from Latin ritus 'rite'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ritualistic 是英语 ritual 加后缀 -istic，后者经拉丁语来自希腊 -istikos「以……方式」。ritual 本身来自拉丁 ritus「仪式」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ritus meant 'a rite, a religious ceremony'. Its deeper origin is uncertain, and the suggested link to a Vedic word for fixed order is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: ritus 意为「仪式、宗教典礼」。其更深来源不确定，把它与吠陀语中「固定秩序」一词相联系只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Ritus plus -alis gave ritualis 'relating to rites', the adjective that English borrowed as ritual.
items.cn: ritus 加 -alis 构成 ritualis「与仪式有关的」，英语借入后作 ritual。

items.en: The suffix -istikos formed adjectives of manner; Latin took it as -isticus, and French and English shortened it to -istic.
items.cn: 后缀 -istikos 构成表方式的形容词；拉丁语吸收为 -isticus，法语与英语再缩短为 -istic。

items.en: English ritualistic first described church parties devoted to elaborate rites in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 英语 ritualistic 在十九世纪最早用来描述热衷繁复礼仪的教会派别。

items.en: Psychology, art criticism and animal behaviour later took the adjective for compulsive, stylized and display behaviour.
items.cn: 心理学、艺术批评与动物行为研究后来用这个形容词指强迫性、风格化与展示性行为。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first use of the psychological sense is not recorded, and the pre-Latin origin of ritus remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：心理学义没有确切的最早书证；ritus 在拉丁语之前的来源仍无定论。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the same stem; group two holds adjectives for related kinds of formality.
note.cn: 第一组是同出这一词干的词；第二组是表示相关形式化程度的形容词。

entries.definition: The rite itself or a plain adjective meaning 'of a rite'; ritualistic adds the idea of manner or excess.
entries.definitionCN: 指仪式本身，或意为「仪式的」的普通形容词；ritualistic 另带方式或过度的意味。

entries.definition: Attachment to rites as a system, or the study of them; it names a tendency, not a manner.
entries.definitionCN: 指对仪式体系的依附或对它的研究；它指倾向，而非方式。

entries.definition: A single prescribed ceremony; the adjective never means 'a ceremony'.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个规定的典礼；这个形容词从不表示「一场典礼」。

entries.definition: The adverb form, used of performing an act in a rite-like manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式，指以仪式般的方式完成某动作。

entries.definition: Relating to an official ceremony; it points to the occasion and its dignity.
entries.definitionCN: 指与正式典礼有关，指向场合及其庄重。

entries.definition: Overly polite and formal in manner, especially between people.
entries.definitionCN: 指举止过分客气正式，尤指人际之间。

entries.definition: Following accepted rules of style; ritualistic is narrower and points to rite-like repetition.
entries.definitionCN: 指遵循公认的形式规则；ritualistic 更窄，指向仪式般的重复。

entries.definition: Carried out as a duty with little interest; ritualistic can imply the same hollowness but stresses form.
entries.definitionCN: 指当作义务草草完成；ritualistic 也可含同样空洞之意，但更强调形式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ritual plus -istic means 'in the manner of a rite'.
normal.cn: ritual 加 -istic 意为「以仪式的方式」。

normal.en: The suffix -istic also builds artistic, characteristically and simplistic.
normal.cn: 后缀 -istic 还构成 artistic、characteristically 与 simplistic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: ritualistic behavior, ritualistic gesture, ritualistic precision.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：仪式化行为、仪式性手势、仪式般的精确。

normal.en: The family runs rite, ritual, ritualistic, ritualism, ritualize and ritualization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 rite、ritual、ritualistic、ritualism、ritualize 与 ritualization。

normal.en: The word is neutral in church history and critical in psychology.
normal.cn: 这个词在教会史中是中性的，在心理学中则带批评。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that repeats the same gesture until the gesture owns the hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手重复同一个手势，直到手势反过来支配了手。

abstract.en: Picture a stage where every step has been decided before the music starts.
abstract.cn: 想象一个舞台，音乐未起，每一步都已被决定。

abstract.en: Picture a form that keeps standing after the meaning has left the room.
abstract.cn: 想象意义离开房间后，形式仍站在原地。

examples.en: The anthropologist noted the ritualistic greeting used at every door.
examples.cn: 人类学家记录了每道门前使用的仪式化问候。

examples.en: His ritualistic cleaning calmed him but exhausted his family.
examples.cn: 他仪式化的清洁让他安心，却让家人疲惫。

examples.en: The film's ritualistic pace divided the audience.
examples.cn: 影片仪式化的节奏让观众分成两派。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ritual（仪式）+ istic（……式的）」——像仪式一样的、按套路来的

root: 英语 ritual（来自拉丁 ritus「仪式」与 ritualis「与仪式有关的」）加后缀 -istic（经拉丁来自希腊 -istikos「以……方式」）。ritus 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one stylistic move: an action is performed as a rite, and that manner is then read as precision, faithfulness, compulsion, art, procedure, empty form and animal display.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个风格化动作展开：一个动作被当作仪式来完成，这种完成方式再依次被读作精确、虔诚、强迫、艺术、流程、空洞形式与动物展示。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand repeating one gesture until the gesture seems to belong to something older than the person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手重复同一个手势，直到这手势仿佛属于比人更古老的东西。

branches.en: THE MANNER: the adjective begins as a description of style, not of belief.
branches.cn: 方式：这个形容词起初描述风格，而非信仰。

branches.en: FIXITY, PRAISED OR BLAMED: the same exactness can look faithful or mechanical.
branches.cn: 固定性，或被赞或被责：同一种精确既可能显得虔诚，也可能显得机械。

branches.en: THE CAGE: when anxiety drives the repetition, the rite becomes a symptom.
branches.cn: 牢笼：当焦虑驱动重复，仪式就变成症状。

branches.en: STAGE AND EMPTY FORM: art borrows the rite's weight, and empty procedure borrows only its shell.
branches.cn: 舞台与空壳：艺术借来仪式的重量，空洞程序只借来外壳。

branches.en: PROCEDURE AND SIGNAL: organizations and animals both repeat a fixed sequence to make a message visible.
