branches.cn: 流程与信号：组织与动物都重复固定序列，让讯息可见。

intro.en: Ritualistic is a Latin stem with two layers of suffix, one Latin and one Greek, and the same stem builds the whole ritual family.
intro.cn: ritualistic 是一个拉丁词干加两层后缀，一层拉丁、一层希腊，同一词干构成整个 ritual 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ritus and ritualis supply the stem; Greek -istikos, taken into Latin as -isticus, supplies the ending of manner.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ritus 与 ritualis 提供词干；希腊 -istikos 经拉丁作 -isticus，提供表方式的后缀。

items.example: The stem names the ceremony behind the manner.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干指方式背后的典礼。

items.example: Ritualis became English ritual.
items.exampleCN: ritualis 变成英语 ritual。

items.example: Ritual is the base of the longer adjective.
items.exampleCN: ritual 是更长形容词的基础。

items.example: The suffix makes manner adjectives.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表方式的形容词。

items.meaning: in the manner of a rite
items.example: The adjective describes how, not why.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述「如何」，不描述「为何」。

items.example: Ritualism names the tendency behind the manner.
items.exampleCN: ritualism 指方式背后的倾向。

items.example: The verb names the act of turning routine into rite.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指把日常程序变成仪式。

items.example: Ritualization is the process the adjective describes.
items.exampleCN: 仪式化正是这个形容词所描述的过程。

items.example: Rite is the shortest member of the family.
items.exampleCN: rite 是这个词族中最短的成员。

items.example: The adverb modifies the performance itself.
items.exampleCN: 副词修饰的是表演本身。

definition_zh: 按既定程序举行的正式典礼；也指典礼上的客套与形式
definition_en: a formal event carried out in a set order, and the formalities or polite behaviour associated with it
core_image: 礼堂门口铺着红毯，两排椅子中间留出一条很窄的通道
scene: 礼堂的门口铺着红毯，两排椅子中间留出一条很窄的通道。The graduation ceremony ended with the whole hall singing the school song.
sceneCN: 这里 ceremony 指「按既定程序举行的正式典礼」（第 1 个义项：有固定顺序的公开仪式）；句意为毕业典礼在全体齐唱校歌中结束。可辨识物件：红毯、椅子、通道、礼堂、校歌单。

senses.title: A formal event in a set order
senses.titleCN: 按既定程序举行的正式活动
senses.definition: an official event whose parts follow a fixed sequence
senses.definitionCN: 各部分按固定顺序进行的正式活动
senses.example: The graduation ceremony ended with the whole hall singing the school song.
senses.exampleCN: 毕业典礼在全体齐唱校歌中结束。
senses.why: the Latin noun named religious worship, and the word still carries the idea of an order that must be followed.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词原指宗教礼拜，至今仍带「必须遵循的顺序」之意。

senses.title: A rite of passage for a person
senses.definition: a ceremony marking birth, coming of age, marriage or death
senses.definitionCN: 标记出生、成年、结婚或死亡的仪式
senses.example: The wedding ceremony was short, but the feast lasted all night.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼很短，宴席却持续了一整夜。
senses.why: the most personal ceremonies mark a change of status, which a community must witness.
senses.whyCN: 最私人的典礼标记身份变化，而这种变化必须由社群见证。

senses.title: A public or state occasion
senses.definition: an official event such as a state opening, a memorial or a signing
senses.definitionCN: 如国家开幕、纪念或签署仪式等官方活动
senses.example: The opening ceremony was broadcast in four languages.
senses.exampleCN: 开幕式用四种语言播出。
senses.why: public ceremonies turn power into something visible and shareable.
senses.whyCN: 公共典礼把权力变成可见、可共享的东西。

senses.title: The ordered acts of worship
senses.definition: the prescribed words and actions of a religious service
senses.definitionCN: 宗教礼拜中规定的言辞与动作
senses.example: A quiet ceremony was held in the chapel before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明前在小教堂举行了一场安静的仪式。
senses.why: this is the oldest layer of the word, and the one from which the others spread.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老的一层，也是其他义项由此扩散的源头。

senses.title: Mere politeness and formality
senses.definition: the polite formalities expected in an interaction, often felt as unnecessary
senses.definitionCN: 交往中被期待的客气形式，常被视为多余
senses.example: There was no ceremony about the handover: one key, one nod.
senses.exampleCN: 交接没有什么客套：一把钥匙，一个点头。
senses.why: when the rite loses its content, what remains is ceremony as pure form.
senses.whyCN: 当仪式失去内容，剩下的就是纯形式的客套。

senses.title: A ceremony of awarding or conferring
senses.titleCN: 授予学位或奖项的典礼
senses.definition: an event at which degrees, prizes or titles are formally conferred
senses.definitionCN: 正式授予学位、奖项或头衔的活动
senses.example: The award ceremony ran late because every winner spoke.
senses.exampleCN: 颁奖典礼拖到很晚，因为每位获奖者都发了言。
senses.why: modern institutions borrow the old rite to make a decision look legitimate.
senses.whyCN: 现代机构借用古老仪式，让一项决定显得正当。

senses.title: The dignity that a rite confers
senses.definition: the seriousness or gravity that surrounds a formal act
senses.definitionCN: 环绕正式行为的严肃与庄重
senses.example: The simple room gained a certain ceremony once the candles were lit.
senses.exampleCN: 蜡烛一点，简朴的房间就有了某种庄重。
senses.why: the word can name an atmosphere as well as an event, since order itself produces gravity.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既可指活动，也可指气氛，因为秩序本身就产生庄严。

senses.title: A traditional community rite
senses.definition: a local rite such as a harvest or initiation ceremony studied by anthropologists
senses.definitionCN: 人类学家研究的丰收礼或成年礼等地方仪式
senses.example: The village still holds a ceremony for the first catch of the season.
senses.exampleCN: 村里仍为当季第一次捕鱼举行仪式。
senses.why: anthropology treats such events as the place where a community states its own rules.
senses.whyCN: 人类学把这类活动视为社群陈述自身规则的场所。

senses.title: The fixed order inside the event
senses.definition: the sequence of parts that makes an event recognizable as a ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 使一场活动可被认出是典礼的各部分顺序
senses.example: The ceremony follows the same order it did a century ago.
senses.exampleCN: 这场典礼的顺序与一个世纪前相同。
senses.why: the word names both the whole event and the order that holds it together.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既指整场活动，也指维系它的那个顺序。

intro.en: Ceremony comes from Latin caerimonia 'religious worship, sacred rite', of uncertain origin and possibly Etruscan, through Old French ceremonie. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ceremony 经古法语 ceremonie 来自拉丁 caerimonia「宗教礼拜、神圣仪式」，其来源不确定，可能出自伊特鲁里亚语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Caerimonia named religious worship and the awe attached to it. Source uncertain: no convincing Latin or Indo-European derivation has been established, and an Etruscan origin is often suggested but not proved.
items.cn: caerimonia 指宗教礼拜以及随之而来的敬畏。来源不确定：尚无令人信服的拉丁或印欧语派生来源，常有人提出源自伊特鲁里亚语，但未获证实。

items.en: Late Latin built the adjective caerimonialis 'belonging to worship', which became English ceremonial.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语构成形容词 caerimonialis「属于礼拜的」，后来成为英语 ceremonial。

items.en: Old French ceremonie carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century, still close to the church sense.
items.cn: 古法语 ceremonie 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，仍接近教会义。

items.en: From the sixteenth century ceremony named court and state occasions as well as church rites.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，ceremony 除教会礼仪外，也指宫廷与国家场合。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the word could mean mere polite form, giving phrases such as without ceremony.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，这个词可指纯粹的客套形式，于是出现 without ceremony 这类短语。

items.en: Source uncertain (origin and first dates): the pre-Latin source of caerimonia is unsettled, and the earliest uses of several extended senses are dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词源与首见年代）：caerimonia 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，若干引申义的最早用法也只有约略年代。

note.en: Group one holds the adjective and adverb forms of the same family; group two holds near synonyms for a formal event.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词族的形容词与副词形式；第二组是表示正式活动的近义词。

entries.definition: Relating to or used in a ceremony; it also names the system of rites as a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指与典礼有关的或典礼上使用的；作名词时也指礼仪体系。

entries.definition: Describes a person or manner that is excessively formal and polite.
entries.definitionCN: 描述人或举止过分正式客气。

entries.definition: The adverb for doing something in a ceremonial way.
entries.definitionCN: 指以典礼方式做某事的副词。

entries.definition: The noun for excessive formality of manner.
entries.definitionCN: 指举止过度拘礼的名词。

entries.definition: A prescribed religious or solemn act; a ceremony may contain many rites.
entries.definitionCN: 指规定的宗教或庄严行为；一场典礼可包含多个仪式。

entries.definition: A formal gathering described without any hint of sacredness.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式聚会，不含任何神圣意味。

entries.definition: A particular time or event; it is broader and need not be formal.
entries.definitionCN: 指特定时刻或事件；范围更广，也不必正式。

entries.definition: A required or conventional procedure; ceremony can mean the whole event, formality only its rules.
entries.definitionCN: 指规定或惯常的程序；ceremony 可指整场活动，formality 只指其规则。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin source meant religious awe, so the word still makes an order feel heavier than ordinary time.
normal.cn: 拉丁语源指宗教敬畏，因此这个词至今让某种秩序比平常时间更沉重。

normal.en: The family runs ceremony, ceremonial, ceremonious, ceremonially and ceremoniousness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ceremony、ceremonial、ceremonious、ceremonially 与 ceremoniousness。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: graduation ceremony, opening ceremony, award ceremony, without ceremony.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：毕业典礼、开幕式、颁奖典礼、不拘礼节地。

normal.en: The phrase stand on ceremony means insisting on polite form when none is needed.
normal.cn: stand on ceremony 意为在本不需要时仍坚持客套。

normal.en: A ceremony has parts; that is why the same word can mean the event and its order.
normal.cn: 典礼由若干部分组成，因此同一个词既可指活动，也可指其顺序。

abstract.en: Picture a red carpet laid down so that a walk becomes a statement.
abstract.cn: 想象一条铺好的红毯，让一段走路变成一句声明。

abstract.en: Picture a clock face whose hands must pass the same marks in the same order.
abstract.cn: 想象一个钟面，指针必须按同样顺序经过同样的刻度。

abstract.en: Picture an empty stage still lit after the performers have gone.
abstract.cn: 想象演员离场后，空舞台的灯仍亮着。

examples.en: The ceremony began with a minute of silence.
examples.cn: 典礼以一分钟默哀开始。

examples.en: They married in a civil ceremony at the town hall.
examples.cn: 他们在市政厅举行了民事婚礼。

examples.en: He handed over the keys without ceremony and left.
examples.cn: 他把钥匙随手交出，没有客套便离开了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ceremony（典礼）」——一场按规矩走完的正式活动

root: 拉丁 caerimonia「宗教礼拜、神圣仪式」（来源不确定，可能出自伊特鲁里亚语）→ 古法语 ceremonie → 英语 ceremony；形容词 caerimonialis 则成为 ceremonial。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one public order: an event is marked off from ordinary time, and that marking is then read as a life rite, a state occasion, worship, empty politeness, an award, an atmosphere, a local custom and the sequence itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个公开秩序展开：一场活动被从平常时间里划出，这种划出再依次被读作人生礼仪、国家场合、礼拜、空洞客套、颁奖、气氛、地方习俗与顺序本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow path left between two rows of chairs, so that walking down it becomes an event.
core.cn: 核心意象：两排椅子之间留出一条窄道，走过它便成了一件大事。

branches.en: THE EVENT AND ITS ORDER: the whole occasion and the sequence that makes it recognizable.
branches.cn: 活动与顺序：整场场合，以及使它可被认出的那个序列。

branches.en: A PERSON IS MOVED: birth, marriage and death are crossings that need witnesses.
branches.cn: 人被移动：出生、婚姻与死亡都是需要见证的跨越。

branches.en: POWER AND WORSHIP: the state and the church both make their authority visible through order.
branches.cn: 权力与礼拜：国家与教会都借秩序让权威可见。

branches.en: A PRIZE IS CONFERRED: the old rite now legitimizes a modern decision.
branches.cn: 授予奖项：古老仪式如今为现代决定提供正当性。

branches.en: SHELL, ATMOSPHERE, LOCAL USE: form can empty out, can fill a room, or can hold a village together.
branches.cn: 外壳、气氛、地方用法：形式可以空洞，可以填满一室，也可以凝聚一个村庄。

intro.en: Ceremony is a Latin noun of uncertain origin whose family grew through one Late Latin adjective and a pair of English suffixes.
intro.cn: ceremony 是一个来源不确定的拉丁名词，其词族通过一个晚期拉丁形容词与几个英语后缀扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin caerimonia and its Late Latin adjective caerimonialis stand behind ceremony and ceremonial; English added -ous, -ly and -ness.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 caerimonia 与晚期拉丁形容词 caerimonialis 是 ceremony 与 ceremonial 的来源；英语又加上 -ous、-ly 与 -ness。

items.example: The noun carried awe as well as order.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词既带秩序，也带敬畏。

items.example: The adjective became the English word ceremonial.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词成为英语 ceremonial。

items.example: The noun widened from church to state.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词从教会扩展到国家。

items.meaning: of a ceremony; the system of rites
items.example: Ceremonial can be an adjective or a noun.
items.exampleCN: ceremonial 既可作形容词也可作名词。

items.example: The suffix adds abundance, then excess.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀先表「充满」，再转为「过度」。

items.example: The tools were ceremonially placed on the table.
items.exampleCN: 工具被按礼仪摆放在桌上。

items.example: The noun names the quality of standing on ceremony.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指拘泥礼节的性质。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a tendency.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成一种倾向。

items.example: The noun names a person, not an event.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指人，不指活动。

definition_zh: 典礼的；仪式上使用的；拘泥礼节的
definition_en: relating to a ceremony, used in a ceremony, or marked by excessive formality
core_image: 宫门前的石阶上铺着长毯，侍卫换上镶金边的礼服
scene: 宫门前的石阶上铺着长毯，侍卫换上镶金边的礼服。The mayor's ceremonial role is to cut the ribbon, not to set the budget.
sceneCN: 这里 ceremonial 指「典礼的、仪式上使用的」（第 1 个义项：属于典礼场合的）；句意为市长这一职位的礼仪性职责是剪彩，而非决定预算。可辨识物件：石阶、长毯、礼服、金边、剪刀。

senses.title: Belonging to a ceremony
senses.definition: connected with a formal ceremony rather than with ordinary use
senses.definitionCN: 与正式典礼相关，而非与日常使用相关
senses.example: The mayor's ceremonial role is to cut the ribbon, not to set the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 市长这一职位的礼仪性职责是剪彩，而非决定预算。
senses.why: the adjective is built from the noun of worship, so it points at the occasion rather than the function.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词由表礼拜的名词构成，因此指向场合而非功能。

senses.title: Used or worn in a ceremony
senses.titleCN: 典礼上使用的（服饰与器物）
senses.definition: describing robes, swords, plates or seats reserved for formal rites
senses.definitionCN: 描述专供正式仪式使用的袍服、剑、器皿或座位
senses.example: The ceremonial sword is kept in a glass case.
senses.exampleCN: 礼仪用剑被保存在玻璃柜中。
senses.why: objects become ceremonial when their use is fixed to one kind of occasion.
senses.whyCN: 当器物的用途被固定于某类场合，它就成了礼仪性的。

senses.title: Stiffly polite in manner
senses.definition: describing behaviour that is more formal than the situation requires
senses.definitionCN: 描述比场合所需更正式的行为
senses.example: Their ceremonial politeness made the small room feel colder.
senses.exampleCN: 他们拘礼的客气让这间小屋显得更冷。
senses.why: the same word can criticize formality when the rite has no real occasion.
senses.whyCN: 当仪式并无真正场合时，同一个词就能批评这种形式化。

senses.title: Official and state ritual
senses.definition: belonging to the formal duties of a state or its officers
senses.definitionCN: 属于国家或其官员的正式职责
senses.example: The president's ceremonial duties include receiving ambassadors.
senses.exampleCN: 总统的礼仪性职责包括接见大使。
senses.why: states separate the power to decide from the ceremony of representing.
senses.whyCN: 国家把决策之权与代表性的礼仪分开。

senses.title: Belonging to religious rite
senses.definition: describing the prescribed forms of worship and its objects
senses.definitionCN: 描述礼拜的规定形式及其器物
senses.example: The ceremonial washing precedes every offering.
senses.exampleCN: 每次献祭之前都要行礼仪性的洗涤。
senses.why: this is the oldest layer, where ceremony meant the awe of worship.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层，当时 ceremony 指礼拜的敬畏。

senses.title: Symbolic without real power
senses.titleCN: 仅有象征意义而无实权的
senses.definition: describing a title or body that performs the forms of authority but does not decide
senses.definitionCN: 描述只履行权威形式却不作决定的头衔或机构
senses.example: The council is largely ceremonial under the new charter.
senses.exampleCN: 根据新宪章，这个议事会基本只是礼仪性的。
senses.why: when power moves elsewhere, the old forms remain as ceremony without content.
senses.whyCN: 当权力转移，旧形式便作为无内容的仪式留存下来。

senses.title: Grand in scale and display
senses.definition: marked by elaborate display, uniform and staging
senses.definitionCN: 以繁复排场、制服与场面调度为特征
senses.example: The ceremonial arrival lasted longer than the talks.
senses.exampleCN: 礼仪性的抵达比会谈本身还长。
senses.why: display is how an occasion makes its importance visible to a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 排场是场合向人群展示重要性的方式。

senses.title: Performed for form rather than use
senses.titleCN: 仪式性动作而非实用的
senses.definition: done as a sign or form, without practical effect
senses.definitionCN: 作为标志或形式完成，没有实际效果
senses.example: The first cut was ceremonial; the machine did the real work.
senses.exampleCN: 第一刀只是仪式性的，真正干活的是机器。
senses.why: the word marks the line between acting out a role and doing the work.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标出演角色与做实事之间的界线。

intro.en: Ceremonial comes from Late Latin caerimonialis 'belonging to worship', from caerimonia 'religious rite', a noun of uncertain and possibly Etruscan origin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ceremonial 来自晚期拉丁 caerimonialis「属于礼拜的」，而该词出自 caerimonia「宗教仪式」，后者来源不确定，可能出自伊特鲁里亚语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Caerimonia named worship and the awe around it. Source uncertain: no convincing Latin or Indo-European derivation is established, and an Etruscan origin is a common suggestion rather than a proof.
items.cn: caerimonia 指礼拜以及围绕它的敬畏。来源不确定：尚无令人信服的拉丁或印欧语派生来源，源自伊特鲁里亚语是常见推测而非证明。

items.en: The suffix -alis formed the adjective 'belonging to worship', used of books, vestments and gestures.
items.cn: 后缀 -alis 构成形容词「属于礼拜的」，用于书籍、法衣与动作。

items.en: Old French ceremonial carried the adjective into English, where it first described church rites and their objects.
items.cn: 古法语 ceremonial 把这个形容词带入英语，最初描述教会礼仪及其器物。

items.en: Courts then borrowed the word for official duties that represent power without exercising it.
items.cn: 此后宫廷借用这个词，指代表权力却不行使权力的正式职责。

items.en: The critical sense 'merely symbolic' grew as constitutional states separated ceremony from decision.
items.cn: 随着宪政国家把礼仪与决策分离，批评性的「只是象征」义随之出现。

items.en: Source uncertain (origin and dates): the pre-Latin source of caerimonia is unsettled, and the first uses of the symbolic sense are dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词源与年代）：caerimonia 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，象征义的最早用法也只有约略年代。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same family that differ in meaning; group two holds words for roles and styles that are easily mixed up with this one.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词族中含义不同的形式；第二组是容易与之混淆的角色与风格词。

entries.definition: The event itself; ceremonial is what belongs to it or what it uses.
entries.definitionCN: 指活动本身；ceremonial 指属于它或它所使用的东西。

entries.definition: Describes a person or manner as stiffly polite; ceremonial can describe objects and roles.
entries.definitionCN: 描述人或举止拘礼；ceremonial 可描述器物与角色。

entries.definition: The adverb, used of performing an act as a rite rather than for use.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，指把某动作当作仪式而非实用行为来完成。

entries.definition: Attachment to ritual forms for their own sake.
entries.definitionCN: 指为形式本身而依附礼仪。

entries.definition: Carrying meaning beyond the act; a ceremonial act is often symbolic, but not every symbol is a rite.
entries.definitionCN: 指承载动作之外的意义；礼仪性动作常是象征性的，但并非每个符号都是仪式。

entries.definition: Holding a title without its powers; it stresses the empty office, not the ritual display.
entries.definitionCN: 指只拥头衔而无实权；强调空衔，而非仪式排场。

entries.definition: Following set rules of style or procedure; ceremonial is narrower and ties form to a rite.
entries.definitionCN: 指遵循既定风格或程序规则；ceremonial 更窄，把形式绑在仪式上。

entries.definition: The ordered act; ceremonial describes what surrounds or belongs to such an act.
entries.definitionCN: 指有序的行为；ceremonial 描述围绕或属于这种行为的事物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ceremonial and ceremony share one Latin noun of worship; -alis made the adjective.
normal.cn: ceremonial 与 ceremony 共用同一个表礼拜的拉丁名词，-alis 构成形容词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: ceremonial role, ceremonial dress, ceremonial duties, ceremonial opening.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：礼仪性职责、礼服、礼仪性职责、剪彩仪式。

normal.en: A ceremonial head of state reigns and represents but does not govern.
normal.cn: 礼仪性国家元首在位并代表国家，但不执政。

normal.en: The family runs ceremony, ceremonial, ceremonious, ceremonially and ceremonialism.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ceremony、ceremonial、ceremonious、ceremonially 与 ceremonialism。

normal.en: Keep ceremonial apart from ceremonious: objects and roles versus stiff politeness.
normal.cn: 要把 ceremonial 与 ceremonious 分开：前者指器物与角色，后者指拘谨的客气。

abstract.en: Picture a golden key that opens nothing but makes everyone stand up.
abstract.cn: 想象一把金钥匙，什么也打不开，却让所有人起立。

abstract.en: Picture a robe heavier than the body inside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一件袍子，比穿它的人还重。

abstract.en: Picture a ribbon cut long after the building is finished.
abstract.cn: 想象大楼早已完工，彩带却才被剪断。

examples.en: The ceremonial welcome included a band and a guard of honour.
examples.cn: 礼仪性的欢迎包括乐队与仪仗队。

examples.en: Her title is ceremonial; the real decisions are made elsewhere.
examples.cn: 她的头衔只是礼仪性的，真正的决定在别处做出。

examples.en: The vessel is ceremonial and never used for drinking.
examples.cn: 这件器皿是礼仪用的，从不用于饮水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ceremony（典礼）+ al（……的）」——典礼上的、礼仪性的

root: 晚期拉丁 caerimonialis「属于礼拜的」，出自 caerimonia「宗教仪式」；caerimonia 来源不确定，可能出自伊特鲁里亚语。经法语进入英语作 ceremonial。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one label: something is set aside for a formal occasion, and that setting-aside is then read as dress, politeness, state duty, worship, empty title, display and pure form.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个标签展开：某物被划归正式场合专用，这种划归再依次被读作服饰、客套、国家职责、礼拜、空衔、排场与纯形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long carpet laid over stone steps, marking a path that is not for everyday traffic.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条铺在石阶上的长毯，标出一条不供日常通行的路。

branches.en: THE OCCASION: the adjective begins by pointing to the ceremony itself.
branches.cn: 场合：这个形容词先指向典礼本身。

branches.en: THINGS SET APART: a robe and a first cut are both removed from ordinary use.
branches.cn: 被划出之物：礼服与第一刀都被移出日常用途。

branches.en: POLITENESS AND SPECTACLE: too much formality can chill a room or fill a square.
branches.cn: 客套与排场：过多的形式既能冷却一室，也能填满广场。

branches.en: THRONE AND ALTAR: state and church both dress their authority in prescribed form.
branches.cn: 王座与祭坛：国家与教会都用规定形式给权威穿衣。

branches.en: THE EMPTY OFFICE: when decision moves away, the forms remain and the word turns critical.
branches.cn: 空衔：当决策移走，形式留下，这个词便带上批评。

intro.en: Ceremonial is a Late Latin adjective built from a noun of uncertain origin, and English later made nouns and adverbs from it.
intro.cn: ceremonial 是一个由来源不确定的名词构成的晚期拉丁形容词，英语后来又以它造出名词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Caerimonia supplied the stem and -alis the relational ending; English added -ly, -ism and -ist to build the rest of the family.
latinIntro.cn: caerimonia 提供词干，-alis 提供关系词尾；英语又加 -ly、-ism 与 -ist 构成词族其余成员。

items.example: The noun named the awe before it named the event.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词先指敬畏，后指活动。

items.example: The suffix makes a relational adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成关系形容词。

items.example: The adjective covered books, robes and gestures.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词涵盖书籍、袍服与动作。

items.meaning: of a ceremony; the system of rites
items.example: English uses it as both adjective and noun.
items.exampleCN: 英语把它兼作形容词与名词。

items.example: The ground was ceremonially swept first.

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a tendency.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成一种倾向。

items.meaning: a person devoted to ritual form
items.example: The noun names a person rather than an event.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指人，不指活动。

items.example: The noun is the base the adjective describes.
items.exampleCN: 名词是形容词所描述的基础。

items.example: The -ous form points at people, not objects.
