definition_zh: 沿袭传统的；传统风格的；老式的
definition_en: following or belonging to a tradition, especially one handed down over generations
core_image: 院子里摆着一排木犁，墙上挂着一把旧琵琶，老人正教孩子按老法子调弦
scene: 院子里摆着一排木犁，墙上挂着一把旧琵琶，老人正教孩子按老法子调弦。The traditional recipe uses only three ingredients and a clay pot.
sceneCN: 这里 traditional 指「沿袭传统的」（第 1 个义项：从上一代传下来并继续遵循的）；句意为这道传统食谱只用三种材料和一只陶罐。可辨识物件：木犁、琵琶、陶罐、调料。

pos.zh: 传统的；传统风格的；老式的

senses.title: Handed down and still followed
senses.titleCN: 从上一代传下并继续遵循的
senses.definition: describing practices that a group receives from earlier generations and keeps using
senses.definitionCN: 描述一个群体从先辈承接并继续使用的做法
senses.example: The traditional recipe uses only three ingredients and a clay pot.
senses.exampleCN: 这道传统食谱只用三种材料和一只陶罐。
senses.why: tradition is a handing over, so the adjective marks what has been passed from hand to hand.
senses.whyCN: tradition 意为「交出、传递」，因此这个形容词标记被一手手传下的东西。

senses.title: In an older architectural or dress style
senses.titleCN: 传统风格的（建筑与服饰）
senses.definition: following the forms, materials or ornament of an earlier period
senses.definitionCN: 沿用较早时期的形式、材料或装饰
senses.example: The house keeps a traditional wooden frame and tiled roof.
senses.exampleCN: 这所房子保留传统的木构架与瓦屋顶。
senses.why: style is the visible trace of a handed-down method, so buildings carry the word easily.
senses.whyCN: 风格是传下来的方法留下的可见痕迹，因此建筑容易带上这个词。

senses.title: By an older method rather than a new one
senses.titleCN: 沿用旧方法的（与创新相对）
senses.definition: using established technique instead of recent or experimental technique
senses.definitionCN: 使用既有技术，而非新近或实验性技术
senses.example: Traditional farming returns nutrients to the soil without chemical fertiliser.
senses.exampleCN: 传统耕作不用化肥，也能把养分还给土壤。
senses.why: the word sets old technique against new, and that contrast is its most common job.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把旧技术与新技术相对，这一对比是它最常见的用途。

senses.title: Belonging to an inherited art form
senses.definition: describing music, dance or craft whose forms are taught within a lineage
senses.definitionCN: 描述在传承谱系内教授形式的音乐、舞蹈或工艺
senses.example: The traditional music of the region uses a two-string instrument.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的传统音乐使用一种两弦乐器。
senses.why: art forms survive by transmission, which is exactly what tradition names.
senses.whyCN: 艺术形式靠传承而存活，而传承正是 tradition 所指。

senses.title: Of inherited values and social rules
senses.titleCN: 传统价值观与社会规范的
senses.definition: describing beliefs about family, duty and conduct received from earlier generations
senses.definitionCN: 描述从先辈承接的关于家庭、义务与行为的信念
senses.example: Traditional values in the village still shape who cares for the elderly.
senses.exampleCN: 村里的传统价值观仍决定由谁照料老人。
senses.why: values are the part of a tradition that people argue about most.
senses.whyCN: 价值观是传统中最常被争论的部分。

senses.title: Of a long-established festival
senses.definition: describing a feast or holiday kept on the same date with the same acts
senses.definitionCN: 描述在同一天以同样活动度过的节期
senses.example: The traditional festival begins with a procession to the river.
senses.exampleCN: 这个传统节日以列队走向河边开始。
senses.why: a calendar is a tradition made visible, so annual feasts are its clearest case.
senses.whyCN: 日历是传统变得可见的形式，因此年度节期是它最清楚的例子。

senses.title: Of long-practised medicine or therapy
senses.definition: describing healing systems based on inherited theory and practice rather than modern trials
senses.definitionCN: 描述基于传承理论与实践的医疗体系，而非现代试验
senses.example: Traditional medicine uses herbs that modern pharmacies rarely stock.
senses.exampleCN: 传统医学使用现代药房很少储备的草药。
senses.why: medicine is one of the fields where the old and the new systems still sit side by side.
senses.whyCN: 医学是旧体系与新体系仍并置的领域之一。

senses.title: Old-fashioned, sometimes disapprovingly
senses.definition: describing attitudes felt to be out of date and unwilling to change
senses.definitionCN: 描述被认为过时且不愿改变的态度
senses.example: His traditional views on office dress annoyed the younger staff.
senses.exampleCN: 他对办公室着装的传统看法让年轻员工不满。
senses.why: the same adjective can praise continuity or blame stiffness, depending on the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词既可赞延续，也可责僵化，取决于说话人。

senses.title: Recognized by long usage
senses.definition: used of a belief or practice accepted because it has long been repeated
senses.definitionCN: 指因长期重复而被接受的看法或做法
senses.example: It is traditional to give the first plate to the eldest guest.
senses.exampleCN: 按传统，第一盘菜要递给最年长的客人。
senses.why: here the word means 'as people have long done', not 'as people have long proved'.
senses.whyCN: 此处这个词意为「人们长久以来的做法」，而非「长久以来的证明」。

intro.en: Traditional is tradition plus the adjective suffix -al. Tradition comes from Latin traditio 'a handing over', from tradere 'to hand over', itself trans- 'across' plus dare 'to give'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: traditional 是 tradition 加形容词后缀 -al。tradition 来自拉丁 traditio「交出、传递」，出自 tradere「交出」，而 tradere 是 trans-「越过」加 dare「给」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Dare meant 'to give'. Its deeper origin is generally traced to the same Indo-European root as English give, though the exact pre-Latin form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: dare 意为「给」。其更深来源一般认为与英语 give 同出一个印欧词根，但拉丁语之前的确切形态属重构形式。

items.en: Trans- 'across' plus dare produced tradere 'to hand over, deliver, betray', literally to give something across to another.
items.cn: trans-「越过」加 dare 构成 tradere「交出、交付、背叛」，字面是把东西递到另一边。

items.en: The noun traditio named a delivery, a surrender, and later a teaching handed down.
items.cn: 名词 traditio 指交付、让与，后来指传下来的教导。

items.en: Old French tradition carried the noun into English, where it named what one generation passes to the next.
items.cn: 古法语 tradition 把这个名词带入英语，指一代传给下一代的东西。

items.en: Tradition plus -al gave traditional in the sixteenth century, first in theology and then in general use.
items.cn: tradition 加 -al 在十六世纪构成 traditional，最初用于神学，后进入一般用法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest uses of the architectural and medical senses are dated only approximately, and the pre-Latin shape of dare is reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：建筑义与医学义的最早用法只有约略年代；dare 在拉丁语之前的形态属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same family; group two holds words that describe inherited or established things from other angles.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词族的不同形式；第二组是从其他角度描述传承或既定事物的词。

entries.definition: The practice or belief itself; traditional is the adjective that says something follows it.
entries.definitionCN: 指被传下的做法或信念本身；traditional 是说明某物遵循它的形容词。

entries.definition: Means 'according to tradition', used to open sentences about long-standing practice.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「按传统」，常用于引出关于长期做法的句子。

entries.definition: A deliberate attachment to tradition as a value, not merely the state of being traditional.
entries.definitionCN: 指有意把传统当作价值来坚持，而不只是处于传统状态。

entries.definition: A person who defends tradition against change.
entries.definitionCN: 指捍卫传统、反对改变的人。

entries.definition: Following what is generally agreed at a given time; tradition looks further back.
entries.definitionCN: 指遵循某一时期普遍同意的东西；tradition 追溯得更远。

entries.definition: Belonging to an acknowledged standard or ancient model, often in art and music.
entries.definitionCN: 指属于公认标准或古代典范，常用于艺术与音乐。

entries.definition: Clearly dated and no longer current; traditional can be neutral or approving.
entries.definitionCN: 明确过时、不再流行；traditional 可以是中性或赞许的。

entries.definition: The whole inherited culture of a group; traditional describes individual things that belong to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个群体继承下来的整体文化；traditional 描述属于它的个别事物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: tradere is trans- 'across' plus dare 'give': a tradition is what was given across the generations.
normal.cn: tradere 是 trans-「越过」加 dare「给」：传统就是跨代递交过来的东西。

normal.en: The family runs tradition, traditional, traditionally, traditionalism and traditionalist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 tradition、traditional、traditionally、traditionalism 与 traditionalist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: traditional culture, traditional methods, traditional medicine, traditional festival.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：传统文化、传统方法、传统医学、传统节日。

normal.en: The adverb traditionally often marks a claim that is customary rather than proven.
normal.cn: 副词 traditionally 常标记一种「按惯例如此」而非已被证明的说法。

normal.en: The word can praise continuity or criticize stiffness, so context decides its colour.
normal.cn: 这个词既可赞延续，也可责僵化，褒贬由语境决定。

abstract.en: Picture a rope passed hand to hand across a river.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子被一手手递过河。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe written in a hand that is not yours.
abstract.cn: 想象一份食谱，字迹不是你的。

abstract.en: Picture a door kept open by the weight of many hands before it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门被许多双先前的手撑着不关。

examples.en: Traditional weaving in the region uses nettle fibre.
examples.cn: 该地区的传统织造使用荨麻纤维。

examples.en: She was raised in a traditional household and left it willingly.
examples.cn: 她在传统家庭中长大，也心甘情愿地离开了它。

examples.en: The festival is traditional, but the date has shifted twice.
examples.cn: 这个节日是传统的，但日期已经变过两次。

root: 拉丁 dare「给」→ trans-「越过」+ dare = tradere「交出、传递」→ traditio「传递、教导」→ 古法语 tradition → 英语 tradition，加 -al 得 traditional。dare 的更深词源一般追溯到与 give 同根，但更早形态属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one gesture: something is handed across generations, and the handover is then read as style, method, art, values, festival, medicine, stubborn age and accepted usage.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个动作展开：某物被跨代递交，这个递交再依次被读作风格、方法、艺术、价值观、节日、医学、守旧与公认用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope passed from hand to hand across a river, each grip trusting the last.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根绳子被一手手递过河，每一握都信任上一握。

branches.en: THE HANDOVER: what is received and what is simply accepted because it is old.
branches.cn: 递交：被承接的东西，以及仅因年久而被人接受的东西。

branches.en: VISIBLE FORM: building and dress show the handover in materials and shapes.
branches.cn: 可见形式：建筑与服饰用材料与形状展示这一递交。

branches.en: OLD TECHNIQUE, OLD REMEDY: farming and healing set inherited practice against modern trial.
branches.cn: 旧技艺与旧疗法：耕作与医疗把传承做法与现代试验相对。

branches.en: INHERITED ART: a lineage teaches a form that outlives its teachers.
branches.cn: 传承艺术：谱系教授一种比教师活得更久的形式。

branches.en: VALUES, CALENDAR, ATTITUDE: beliefs, annual feasts and stubborn views are all inheritances people argue about.
branches.cn: 价值、日历与态度：信念、年度节庆与固执看法都是人们会争论的遗产。

intro.en: Traditional is a Latin verb stem with a Latin prefix and two suffixes, and the same material builds the whole tradition family.
intro.cn: traditional 由一个拉丁动词词干、一个拉丁前缀与两个后缀构成，同一批材料构成整个 tradition 词族。

latinIntro.en: Trans- and dare built tradere; -tio built the noun and -al the English adjective.
latinIntro.cn: trans- 与 dare 构成 tradere；-tio 构成名词，-al 构成英语形容词。

items.example: The prefix makes the giving a movement across.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使「给」成为一次跨过。

items.structure: dare, dedi, datum (Latin verb, first conjugation)
items.example: Dare is the simple act inside the compound.
items.exampleCN: dare 是复合词里那个简单的动作。

items.example: Tradere adds direction to the gift.
items.exampleCN: tradere 给「给」加上了方向。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成表行为的名词。

items.meaning: a delivery; a teaching handed down
items.example: Traditio moved from property to teaching.
items.exampleCN: traditio 从财产交付转向教导传递。

items.example: The noun names the heirloom, not the hand.
items.exampleCN: 名词指传家之物，而非那只手。

items.example: The suffix makes the adjective from the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由名词构成形容词。

items.example: The adjective describes anything the handover reaches.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述递交所触及的一切。

items.example: The suffix turns an attitude into a position.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把态度变成立场。

items.example: The noun names the person who holds the rope.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指握住那根绳子的人。

definition_zh: 习俗；个人习惯；惠顾；（复数）海关与关税；定制的
definition_en: a habitual practice of a group or person, and related senses of patronage, import duty and made-to-order goods
core_image: 老街的铺子门口挂着一块木牌，柜台后的人正按客人的尺寸裁布
scene: 老街的铺子门口挂着一块木牌，柜台后的人正按客人的尺寸裁布。It is the custom here to bring a small gift when you visit a neighbour.
sceneCN: 这里 custom 指「地方沿袭的习俗」（第 1 个义项：群体长期重复的做法）；句意为在这里拜访邻居时带一份小礼物是习俗。可辨识物件：木牌、布匹、尺子、柜台。

senses.title: A habitual practice of a community
senses.definition: a way of behaving that a group has long followed and expects its members to follow
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体长期遵循并期待成员遵循的行为方式
senses.example: It is the custom here to bring a small gift when you visit a neighbour.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里拜访邻居时带一份小礼物是习俗。
senses.why: custom comes from Latin consuetudo 'habit', so its core is repeated use rather than law.
senses.whyCN: custom 来自拉丁 consuetudo「习惯」，核心是反复使用，而非法律。

senses.title: A distinctive local usage
senses.definition: a practice found in one place or people and marking them as different
senses.definitionCN: 见于某一地方或民族、并使他们显得不同的做法
senses.example: The custom of lighting lamps at the door is local to the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 在门口点灯这一习俗只流行于沿海。
senses.why: the same word can name a whole habit or one distinctive instance of it.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既可指整套习惯，也可指其中一个有特色的实例。

senses.title: A personal habit
senses.definition: a small repeated practice belonging to one person rather than a group
senses.definitionCN: 属于某个人而非某个群体的重复小习惯
senses.example: His custom was to read the last page first.
senses.exampleCN: 他的习惯是先读最后一页。
senses.why: the word does not require a crowd; one person can keep a custom too.
senses.whyCN: 这个词并不要求人群，一个人也可以有自己的习惯。

senses.title: An established way of doing things
senses.definition: the usual procedure accepted in a trade, office or ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 在某行业、机构或仪式中被接受的通常程序
senses.example: By custom, the youngest member speaks first.
senses.exampleCN: 按惯例，最年轻的成员先发言。
senses.why: procedure is habit written down, and custom is the older word for it.
senses.whyCN: 程序是写下来的习惯，而 custom 是更古老的说法。

senses.title: Patronage of a shop or business
senses.definition: the regular buying of goods or services from one seller
senses.definitionCN: 长期向同一卖家购买商品或服务
senses.example: The baker lost custom when the road was closed.
senses.exampleCN: 道路封闭后，面包店失去了顾客。
senses.why: custom as habitual use became the word for the people who come habitually.
senses.whyCN: 「习惯性使用」义后来指习惯性前来的人。

senses.title: Import duties and the customs service
senses.definition: the tax charged on imported goods, and the office that collects it
senses.definitionCN: 对进口货物征收的税，以及征收该税的机构
senses.example: The parcels were held at customs for two days.
senses.exampleCN: 包裹在海关扣留了两天。
senses.why: a customary toll became a fixed duty, and the plural froze that sense.
senses.whyCN: 一种惯例性的通行费变成固定税项，复数形式冻结了这一义。

senses.title: Made to order rather than standard
senses.definition: describing goods built to a buyer's measurements or specifications
senses.definitionCN: 描述按买家的尺寸或要求制作的商品
senses.example: He ordered a custom suit for the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 他为典礼定做了一套西装。
senses.why: what is made to one's own habit is literally made to custom, hence bespoke.
senses.whyCN: 按自己的习惯制作，字面上就是「按定制」制作，因此有 bespoke 之义。

senses.title: Practice recognized in law or trade
senses.titleCN: 法律或行业中被承认的惯例
senses.definition: a long-standing practice that courts or professions treat as binding
senses.definitionCN: 法院或行业视为有约束力的长期做法
senses.example: Custom still governs the allocation of water in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 山谷里的用水分配仍由惯例支配。
senses.why: before statutes, custom was the law, and the word kept that authority.
senses.whyCN: 在成文法之前，惯例就是法律，这个词保留了那份权威。

senses.title: The habitual thing one does
senses.definition: used in the pattern it is one's custom to do something
senses.definitionCN: 用于「某人习惯做某事」这一句式
senses.example: It was her custom to walk the same route every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 她习惯每天傍晚走同一条路。
senses.why: the singular count noun here points at one repeated act, not a whole culture.
senses.whyCN: 这里的单数可数名词指一项重复行为，而非整套文化。

intro.en: Custom comes from Old French costume, from Latin consuetudo 'habit, usage', built on consuescere 'to accustom'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: custom 来自古法语 costume，出自拉丁 consuetudo「习惯、惯例」，后者由 consuescere「使习惯」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Suescere meant 'to become used or accustomed'. Its deeper origin is uncertain, and the proposed link to a root meaning 'self' is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: suescere 意为「变得习惯」。其更深来源不确定，把它与某个意为「自身」的词根相联系只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Con- 'thoroughly' plus suescere produced consuescere 'to accustom, to make familiar by use'.
items.cn: con-「彻底」加 suescere 构成 consuescere「使习惯、因反复使用而熟悉」。

items.en: The noun consuetudo named habit, usage and customary right; Roman law already used it for practice treated as binding.
items.cn: 名词 consuetudo 指习惯、惯例与习惯法上的权利；罗马法已用它指被视为有约束力的做法。

items.en: Old French costume meant both 'habit' and 'usual practice', and English borrowed it in both senses.
items.cn: 古法语 costume 同时指「习惯」与「惯常做法」，英语把两个义项都借入。

items.en: English custom kept the social sense, while costume came to mean dress; customer and customs grew from the same root along separate paths.
items.cn: 英语 custom 保留社会义，costume 则转指服装；customer 与 customs 从同一词根沿不同路径发展。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the exact origin of the duty sense and the first use of the made-to-order sense are not recorded, and the pre-Latin origin of suescere is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：关税义的确切来源与定制义的最早用法均无书证；suescere 在拉丁语之前的来源也无定论。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike forms from the same root with sharply different meanings; group two holds near synonyms for repeated practice.
note.cn: 第一组是同根但含义差别很大的形近形式；第二组是表示重复做法的近义词。

entries.definition: The plural is frozen as the name of the duty and the office that collects it, not a plural of habits.
entries.definitionCN: 复数已固化为关税与征税机构的名称，并非「多种习俗」的复数。

entries.definition: One who comes habitually to a shop; the same root moved from practice to people.
entries.definitionCN: 指习惯性来店的人；同一词根从做法转向人。

entries.definition: The same Old French word, now meaning clothing, especially for a role or period.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个古法语词，今指服装，尤指角色或某时代的服装。

entries.definition: Means 'according to custom'; it describes a practice while custom names it.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「按习俗的」；它描述做法，custom 则指做法本身。

entries.definition: A settled tendency of one person; custom usually implies a group and a social expectation.
entries.definitionCN: 指个人固定的倾向；custom 通常含群体与社会期待之意。

entries.definition: The usual way a thing is done; it is neutral and need not be old.
entries.definitionCN: 指做事的通常方式；中性，且不必古老。

entries.definition: A rule accepted by agreement, often recent; custom is older and unwritten.
entries.definitionCN: 指经同意接受的规则，往往较新；custom 更古老且不成文。

entries.definition: Anything passed between generations; custom stresses repeated practice more than age.
entries.definitionCN: 指代代相传的一切；custom 更强调反复实践，而非年代。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: consuetudo is con- 'thoroughly' plus suescere 'become used': a custom is what a group has thoroughly grown used to.
normal.cn: consuetudo 是 con-「彻底」加 suescere「变得习惯」：习俗就是群体彻底习惯了的东西。

normal.en: The family runs custom, customary, customer, customize, customization and customs.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 custom、customary、customer、customize、customization 与 customs。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: local custom, social custom, as is the custom, custom-made.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：地方习俗、社会习俗、按照惯例、定制的。

normal.en: customs with a plural -s means the border agency, not several habits.
normal.cn: 带复数 -s 的 customs 指海关机构，而不是多种习俗。

normal.en: The adjective customary is the neutral partner of the noun.
normal.cn: 形容词 customary 是名词的中性搭档。

abstract.en: Picture a path worn into grass by feet that never asked permission.
abstract.cn: 想象一条被脚步磨进草地的小路，那些脚从未征求许可。

abstract.en: Picture a shop that knows your name before you say it.
abstract.cn: 想象一家你还没开口就知道你名字的店。

abstract.en: Picture a rule kept alive only because everyone keeps repeating it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条规则仅因所有人不断重复而活着。

examples.en: In that town it is the custom to close shops at noon.
examples.cn: 在那个镇上，正午关店是习俗。

examples.en: The tailor will make you a custom jacket in a week.
examples.cn: 裁缝一周内就能为你定做一件外套。

examples.en: Officers at customs opened every third crate.
examples.cn: 海关人员每三只板条箱抽开一只。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「custom（习俗）」——大家一直这么干，就成了规矩

root: 拉丁 suescere「变得习惯」→ con- + suescere = consuescere「使习惯」→ consuetudo「习惯、惯例」→ 古法语 costume → 英语 custom。suescere 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one habit: a practice is repeated until it is expected, and that repetition then appears as local colour, personal routine, procedure, paying customers, import duty and goods made to measure.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个习惯展开：一种做法被重复到成为期待，这种重复再依次表现为地方色彩、个人习惯、程序、惠顾的顾客、进口税与按尺寸制作的商品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a path worn into grass by feet that never needed a sign.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条被脚步磨出的草径，从未需要路标。

branches.en: THE PRACTICE AND ITS COLOUR: a general habit and the local version that marks a place.
branches.cn: 做法与地方色彩：普遍习惯，以及标记一方水土的地方版本。

branches.en: ONE PERSON'S REPETITION: the same word covers a private habit, a procedure and a single repeated act.
branches.cn: 一个人的重复：同一个词涵盖私人习惯、程序与单项重复行为。

branches.en: TRUST AND AUTHORITY: habitual buying and binding practice both rest on long use.
branches.cn: 信任与权威：习惯性购买与有约束力的惯例都依靠长期使用。

branches.en: THE TOLL BOX: a customary payment hardens into a duty with an office behind it.
branches.cn: 收费亭：惯例性的付费硬化为税项，并生出征税机构。

branches.en: MADE TO YOUR HABIT: goods shaped to one buyer's measure are literally made to custom.
branches.cn: 按你的习惯制作：按某位买家尺寸制成的商品，字面上就是按定制而做。

intro.en: Custom is a Latin noun that lost its Latin ending in French, and its root also builds words for buyers and border taxes.
intro.cn: custom 是一个在法语中丢掉拉丁词尾的拉丁名词，其词根还构成表示买家与边境税的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin suescere and consuetudo supplied the stem; Old French costume reshaped the ending, and English added -er, -ary and -ize.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 suescere 与 consuetudo 提供词干；古法语 costume 重塑词尾，英语又加 -er、-ary 与 -ize。

items.meaning: to become used, to be accustomed
items.example: The root carries the idea of growing used to something.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「对某物逐渐习惯」的意思。

items.example: The prefix intensifies the becoming used.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀加强「变得习惯」的程度。

items.example: The verb makes habit into a process.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把习惯变成过程。

items.example: Roman law treated consuetudo as binding.
items.exampleCN: 罗马法把惯例视为有约束力。

items.example: The French word split into two English words.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语词分化成两个英语词。

items.example: Custom kept the social sense.
items.exampleCN: custom 保留了社会义。

items.example: The suffix builds customary from custom.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由 custom 构成 customary。

items.example: The agent suffix turns practice into a person.
items.exampleCN: 施事后缀把做法变成人。

items.example: Customize means to make to a buyer's custom.
items.exampleCN: customize 意为按买家的习惯定制。

items.example: The plural froze into a single administrative sense.
items.exampleCN: 复数固化为单一的行政义。

latinEntries.meaning: to become used, to be accustomed

definition_zh: 惯常的；按习俗的；法律上以惯例为依据的
definition_en: usual because it is established by custom, and in law based on long-standing practice rather than statute
core_image: 村口的路上，来往的人见到长辈都会停下来说一句话
scene: 村口的路上，来往的人见到长辈都会停下来说一句话。It is customary to remove your shoes before entering the shrine.
sceneCN: 这里 customary 指「按习俗的、惯常的」（第 1 个义项：因长期惯例而成为通常做法）；句意为进神龛前脱鞋是惯常的礼俗。可辨识物件：村口、神龛、鞋、石阶。

pos.zh: 惯常的；按习俗的；习惯法上的

senses.title: Usual because custom requires it
senses.titleCN: 因习俗而成为通常做法的
senses.definition: describing what people normally do because long practice expects it
senses.definitionCN: 描述人们因长期惯例的期待而通常做的事
senses.example: It is customary to remove your shoes before entering the shrine.
senses.exampleCN: 进神龛前脱鞋是惯常的礼俗。
senses.why: custom plus -ary means 'according to custom', so the adjective reports an expectation rather than a law.
senses.whyCN: custom 加 -ary 意为「按习俗的」，因此这个形容词报告一种期待，而非法律。

senses.title: Expected in a social exchange
senses.definition: describing the greeting, gift or thanks that a situation calls for
senses.definitionCN: 描述某场合所要求的问候、礼物或致谢
senses.example: A customary bow followed the introduction.
senses.exampleCN: 介绍之后行了一个惯常的鞠躬礼。
senses.why: social life runs on small expectations, and the word marks them as normal.
senses.whyCN: 社会生活靠细小的期待运转，这个词把它们标记为正常。

senses.title: Based on practice in law
senses.titleCN: 法律上以惯例为依据的
senses.definition: describing rights or rules that courts recognize because they have long been practised
senses.definitionCN: 描述法院因长期实践而承认的权利或规则
senses.example: Customary rights to the fishing ground predate the statute.
senses.exampleCN: 对渔场的习惯权利早于成文法存在。
senses.why: before written law, practice was law, and the adjective preserves that authority.
senses.whyCN: 在成文法之前，实践就是法律，这个形容词保留了那份权威。

senses.title: Recognized in international law
senses.definition: describing rules that states follow consistently and treat as legally binding
senses.definitionCN: 描述各国一贯遵循并视为有法律约束力的规则
senses.example: Customary international law binds states that never signed the treaty.
senses.exampleCN: 习惯国际法约束那些从未签署条约的国家。
senses.why: international law borrowed the idea that repeated conduct can create an obligation.
senses.whyCN: 国际法借用了「反复行为可以产生义务」这一观念。

senses.title: Ordinary or average
senses.definition: used of a normal amount of time or effort, without any ritual weight
senses.definitionCN: 指通常的时间或努力程度，不带仪式分量
senses.example: The repair took the customary two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这次维修花了通常的两小时。
senses.why: the word can weaken into 'as usual', once the habit is no longer noticed.
senses.whyCN: 当习惯不再被注意，这个词就可弱化为「照常」。

senses.title: Belonging to a traditional rite
senses.definition: describing the acts that a local ceremony normally includes
senses.definitionCN: 描述地方仪式通常包含的动作
senses.example: The customary offering is rice, salt and clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 惯常的供品是米、盐与清水。
senses.why: rites are the place where custom is most strictly expected.
senses.whyCN: 仪式是习俗被要求得最严格的地方。

senses.title: Socially expected of a person
senses.definition: describing behaviour that others assume a person in a role will show
senses.definitionCN: 描述他人假定某一角色者会表现出的行为
senses.example: It was customary for the host to walk guests to the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 主人送客到门口是惯常的做法。
senses.why: a role carries expectations, and the adjective names them without making them rules.
senses.whyCN: 角色自带期待，这个形容词指出这些期待，却不把它们变成规则。

senses.title: The quality of being conventional
senses.definition: the state of being usual by custom, used in legal and social description
senses.definitionCN: 因习俗而成为通常状态的性质，用于法律与社会描述
senses.example: Lawyers debated the customariness of the old route.
senses.exampleCN: 律师们争论这条古道的惯常性。
senses.why: once a practice is disputed, its quality of being customary must itself be argued.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某种做法有争议，它「是否属于惯例」这一性质本身就要被论证。

intro.en: Customary comes from Medieval Latin consuetudinarius 'according to custom', from consuetudo 'habit', and reached English through Old French coutumier. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: customary 来自中世纪拉丁 consuetudinarius「按习俗的」，出自 consuetudo「习惯」，经古法语 coutumier 进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Consuetudo meant 'habit, usage, customary right', built on consuescere 'to accustom'. Its deeper root suescere 'become used' is of uncertain origin.
items.cn: consuetudo 意为「习惯、惯例、习惯法权利」，由 consuescere「使习惯」构成。其更深词根 suescere「变得习惯」来源不确定。

items.en: The suffix -arius formed adjectives and nouns of belonging, giving consuetudinarius 'according to custom'.
items.cn: 后缀 -arius 构成表归属的形容词与名词，于是有 consuetudinarius「按习俗的」。

items.en: Old French coutumier carried the adjective into English, where it described local rules and personal habits alike.
items.cn: 古法语 coutumier 把这个形容词带入英语，既描述地方规则，也描述个人习惯。

items.en: English courts used customary for rights proved by long practice, as opposed to rights granted by statute.
items.cn: 英国法院用 customary 指由长期实践证明的权利，与成文法授予的权利相对。

items.en: Modern international law extended the word to rules formed by consistent state conduct.
items.cn: 现代国际法把这个词扩展到由各国一贯行为形成的规则。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest legal uses of the English adjective are dated only approximately, and the pre-Latin origin of suescere is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个英语形容词最早的法学用法只有约略年代；suescere 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike forms of the same root; group two holds near synonyms for what is normally done.
note.cn: 第一组是同根的形近形式；第二组是表示「通常如此」的近义词。

entries.definition: The practice itself; customary is the adjective saying something follows it.
entries.definitionCN: 指做法本身；customary 是说明某事物遵循它的形容词。

entries.definition: A habitual buyer, from the same root in its sense of habitual use; it has nothing to do with rules.
entries.definitionCN: 指习惯性买家，同根但取「习惯性使用」义，与规则无关。

entries.definition: The same Old French source, now meaning clothing rather than practice.
entries.definitionCN: 同一古法语来源，今指服装而非做法。

entries.definition: Means 'as is usual', used to soften a statement about normal practice.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「按照惯例」，用来缓和关于通常做法的陈述。

entries.definition: Happening most often, with no reference to custom or law.
entries.definitionCN: 指最常发生，不涉及习俗或法律。

entries.definition: Following accepted social style, often in a slightly critical tone.
entries.definitionCN: 指遵循被接受的社会风格，常带轻微批评口吻。

entries.definition: Describing a repeated personal behaviour, often hard to break.
entries.definitionCN: 描述个人反复的行为，常难以改掉。

entries.definition: Conforming to what is expected in general; customary is narrower and ties expectation to tradition.
entries.definitionCN: 指符合一般期待；customary 更窄，把期待绑在传统上。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: consuetudo 'habit' plus -arius 'belonging to' gives 'belonging to habit', then 'according to custom'.
normal.cn: consuetudo「习惯」加 -arius「属于……的」，先得「属于习惯的」，再得「按习俗的」。

normal.en: The family runs custom, customary, customarily, customariness and customer.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 custom、customary、customarily、customariness 与 customer。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: customary practice, customary law, customary rights, as is customary.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：惯常做法、习惯法、习惯上的权利、按照惯例。

normal.en: Customary law is law proved by long practice, not by a written statute.
normal.cn: 习惯法是由长期实践证明的法律，而非成文法规。

normal.en: The adverb customarily usually means 'as people normally do', not 'as the law requires'.
normal.cn: 副词 customarily 通常意为「人们通常这样做」，而非「法律要求这样」。

abstract.en: Picture a greeting performed before anyone decides to perform it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个问候，在任何人决定做它之前就已经被做了。

abstract.en: Picture a rule with no book, only many mornings.
abstract.cn: 想象一条没有书本、只有许多个早晨的规则。

abstract.en: Picture a road that became official only because everyone kept walking it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路，只因所有人一直走，才成了正式的路。

examples.en: It is customary to bring the host a small gift.
examples.cn: 给主人带一份小礼物是惯常做法。

examples.en: Customary law still governs land in many rural districts.
examples.cn: 在许多乡村地区，土地仍由习惯法管辖。

examples.en: The ceremony followed its customary order without a single change.
examples.cn: 典礼按惯常顺序进行，毫无改动。

root: 中世纪拉丁 consuetudinarius「按习俗的」，出自拉丁 consuetudo「习惯、惯例」，后者由 con- + suescere 构成；经古法语 coutumier 进入英语。suescere 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one expectation: a practice is treated as normal, and that normality is then read as social courtesy, legal right, international rule, mere averageness, ritual form and disputed customariness.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个期待展开：一种做法被视为正常，这种正常再依次被读作社交礼节、法律权利、国际规则、平常程度、仪式形式与有争议的惯常性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a greeting performed before anyone decides to perform it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个问候，在任何人决定做它之前就已经被做了。

branches.en: THE BASE: what people normally do because long practice expects it.
branches.cn: 基础：人们因长期惯例的期待而通常做的事。

branches.en: COURTESY AND RITE: a bow and an offering are the same expectation in different settings.
branches.cn: 礼节与仪式：鞠躬与献供是同一期待在不同场合的表现。

branches.en: FROM COURT TO TREATY: practice becomes a right, and consistent conduct becomes binding law.
branches.cn: 从法庭到条约：实践变成权利，一贯行为变成有约束力的法律。

branches.en: THE ROLE: others assume a person will behave as the position expects.
branches.cn: 角色：他人假定某人会按这个位置所期待的方式行事。

branches.en: THE FADED AND THE DISPUTED: habit can weaken into 'ordinary', or become a quality that must be argued in court.
branches.cn: 淡化与争议：习惯可弱化为「平常」，也可变成必须在法庭上论证的性质。

intro.en: Customary adds a Latin relational suffix to the Latin noun of habit, and English later added -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: customary 在拉丁「习惯」名词上加了拉丁关系后缀，英语后来又加 -ly 与 -ness。

latinIntro.en: Consuetudo supplied the stem and -arius the relational ending; Old French reshaped it into coutumier before English borrowed the word.
latinIntro.cn: consuetudo 提供词干，-arius 提供关系词尾；古法语先把它改写为 coutumier，英语再借入。

items.example: The stem names the practice behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干指形容词背后的做法。

items.example: The suffix makes a relational adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成关系形容词。

items.example: Medieval lawyers used it of local rules.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪法学家用它指地方规则。

items.example: French shortened the long Latin ending.
items.exampleCN: 法语缩短了冗长的拉丁词尾。

items.example: English kept the legal and everyday senses together.
items.exampleCN: 英语把法律义与日常义保留在一起。

items.example: Customarily means in the customary way.
items.exampleCN: customarily 意为以惯常方式。

items.example: Customariness is the quality of being customary.
items.exampleCN: customariness 是「属于惯例」的性质。

items.example: The noun is the base of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 名词是形容词的基础。

items.example: The -er form points at a person, not a rule.
items.exampleCN: -er 形式指向人，而非规则。

definition_zh: 民间世代口耳相传的故事、歌谣、信仰与习俗的总称
definition_en: the traditional stories, songs, beliefs and customs of a community, passed on by word of mouth
core_image: 村口的老槐树下，几个孩子围着一位老人，听他讲一个没有书的故事
scene: 村口的老槐树下，几个孩子围着一位老人，听他讲一个没有书的故事。The folklore of the valley survives mainly in songs sung at harvest.
sceneCN: 这里 folklore 指「民间口耳相传的故事与习俗之总称」（第 1 个义项：一个社群传下来的口头传统）；句意为这个山谷的民间文化主要靠丰收时唱的歌流传。可辨识物件：老槐树、老人、孩子、歌谱。

senses.title: A community's oral inheritance
senses.titleCN: 社群口耳相传的文化遗产
senses.definition: the body of stories, songs and customs that a community passes on without writing them down
senses.definitionCN: 一个社群在不依靠书写的情况下传递的故事、歌谣与习俗整体
senses.example: The folklore of the valley survives mainly in songs sung at harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷的民间文化主要靠丰收时唱的歌流传。
senses.why: folk names the people and lore names what they teach, so the compound is learning that lives in a community rather than a library.
senses.whyCN: folk 指民众，lore 指他们所教的东西，因此这个复合词指活在社群中而非图书馆里的学问。

senses.title: Traditional tales and legends
senses.definition: narrative folklore such as fairy tales, ghost stories and local legends
senses.definitionCN: 如童话、鬼故事与地方传说这类叙事性民俗
senses.example: Every village tells a folklore tale about the old bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 每个村庄都有一则关于那座旧桥的民间故事。
senses.why: stories are the part of folklore that travels furthest without being written.
senses.whyCN: 故事是民俗中最能在不书写的情况下远行传播的部分。

senses.title: Songs and ballads
senses.definition: sung folklore, including work songs, laments and ballads
senses.definitionCN: 歌唱形态的民俗，包括劳动号子、挽歌与叙事歌谣
senses.example: The folklore of the fishing villages is carried by work songs.
senses.exampleCN: 渔村的民间文化由劳动号子承载。
senses.why: melody is a memory aid, so song is the oldest archive of the unschooled.
senses.whyCN: 旋律是记忆的助手，因此歌谣是未受教育者最古老的档案。

senses.title: Popular beliefs and superstitions
senses.definition: unwritten beliefs about luck, spirits, omens and protective practices
senses.definitionCN: 关于运气、鬼魂、预兆与护身做法的成文之外的信念
senses.example: Folklore about the crossroads kept travellers from walking at night.
senses.exampleCN: 关于十字路口的民间说法让旅人不敢夜行。
senses.why: beliefs explain misfortune cheaply, and folklore stores them where no doctrine reaches.
senses.whyCN: 信念能廉价地解释不幸，而民俗把它们储存在教义触及不到之处。

senses.title: Craft and material folk culture
senses.definition: traditional making of tools, cloth, food and dwellings
senses.definitionCN: 工具、织物、食物与居所的传统制作方式
senses.example: The museum collects folklore in the form of baskets and looms.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆以篮子与织机的形式收藏民间工艺。
senses.why: lore is not only told but made, and objects carry instruction in their shape.
senses.whyCN: 学问不只靠讲述，也靠制作，器物在形状里携带技艺。

senses.title: The object of a scholarly discipline
senses.definition: the material that folklorists collect, classify and interpret
senses.definitionCN: 民俗学者采集、分类与解释的材料
senses.example: The journal treats folklore as evidence, not as quaint decoration.
senses.exampleCN: 该期刊把民俗当作证据，而非古雅的装饰。
senses.why: once a field has a name for its material, the material becomes an object of study.
senses.whyCN: 当一个领域为自己的材料命名，这些材料就成了研究对象。

senses.title: The oral tradition of one group
senses.definition: the specific verbal inheritance of a people, region or occupation
senses.definitionCN: 某个民族、地区或职业特有的口头遗产
senses.example: Miners kept their own folklore of underground spirits.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工有自己的地下神灵传说。
senses.why: occupations form their own risk-sharing culture with its own stories.
senses.whyCN: 职业会形成自己的风险分担文化，也有自己的故事。

senses.title: Folk creation in the internet age
senses.definition: jokes, memes and stories that spread anonymously online in the old folk manner
senses.definitionCN: 以古老民间方式在网上匿名传播的笑话、模因与故事
senses.example: Researchers now study the folklore of message boards.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者如今研究论坛上的民间创作。
senses.why: the medium changed, but anonymous communal retelling is the same act as before.
senses.whyCN: 媒介变了，但匿名集体复述仍是同一种行为。

senses.title: A story dismissed as untrue
senses.titleCN: 被当作「传说」的不实说法
senses.definition: used dismissively of a claim that people repeat without evidence
senses.definitionCN: 轻蔑地指人们无证据却反复传播的说法
senses.example: The idea that the tower has no foundations is pure folklore.
senses.exampleCN: 说那座塔没有地基纯粹是民间传说。
senses.why: when a repeated story is doubted, folklore becomes a word for unverified belief.
senses.whyCN: 当反复流传的故事受到怀疑，folklore 就变成「未经证实的说法」之词。

intro.en: Folklore is a deliberately coined English compound: folk, from Old English folc 'people', plus lore, from Old English lār 'teaching, learning'. It was proposed in 1846. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: folklore 是一个有意造出的英语复合词：folk 来自古英语 folc「民众」，lore 来自古英语 lār「教导、学问」。这个词于 1846 年被提出。年代均为约数。

items.en: Folc meant 'people, crowd, tribe'. The pre-Germanic shape is reconstructed, so the earlier form is not witnessed in any text.
items.cn: folc 意为「民众、人群、部族」。日耳曼语之前的形态属重构形式，更早的词形没有任何文本书证。

items.en: Lār meant 'teaching, instruction, learning', and still survives in lore and in learned.
items.cn: lār 意为「教导、传授、学问」，仍存于 lore 与 learned 之中。

items.en: In 1846 William Thoms proposed folklore to replace 'popular antiquities', and the word spread quickly through learned journals.
items.cn: 1846 年威廉·汤姆斯提出用 folklore 取代「民间古物」一词，这个词很快在学术刊物中传播。

items.en: It first meant the whole inherited culture of ordinary people, then narrowed to stories, songs and beliefs, then widened again to include craft and online creation.
items.cn: 它先指普通民众继承的整体文化，后收窄到故事、歌谣与信念，再扩展到工艺与网络创作。

items.en: The word now also serves as a mild dismissal of a claim that circulates without evidence.
items.cn: 如今这个词也用来轻微否定一种无证据却流传的说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Germanic origin): the older Germanic shape of folc is a reconstruction, and the pre-Germanic source of lār is not established.
items.cn: 来源不确定（日耳曼语之前的来源）：folc 更早的日耳曼语形态属重构形式；lār 在日耳曼语之前的来源无定论。

note.en: Group one holds forms built from the two halves of the compound; group two holds narrative or traditional genres often mistaken for it.
note.cn: 第一组是由复合词两半构成的词；第二组是常被与之混淆的叙事或传统类别。

entries.definition: Ordinary people or a particular people; folklore is what they pass on.
entries.definitionCN: 指普通民众或某一民族；folklore 是他们传下的东西。

entries.definition: Traditional knowledge on a subject, as in plant lore or seafaring lore.
entries.definitionCN: 指某一方面的传统知识，如植物知识或航海知识。

entries.definition: A person who collects and studies folklore; the suffix -ist names the person, not the material.
entries.definitionCN: 指采集与研究民俗的人；后缀 -ist 指人，而非材料。

entries.definition: Means 'of folklore', often used of art that borrows folk material.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「民间文化的」，常用于借用民间素材的艺术。

entries.definition: A story about a person or place, told as if historical; folklore is the whole field that contains it.
entries.definitionCN: 指关于某人或某地、仿佛历史般讲述的故事；folklore 是包含它的整个领域。

entries.definition: A story about gods or origins, usually tied to belief; folklore can be secular and everyday.
entries.definitionCN: 指关于神祇或起源的故事，通常与信仰相连；folklore 可以是世俗日常的。

entries.definition: Anything passed between generations, including law and craft; folklore stresses oral and communal forms.
entries.definitionCN: 指代代相传的一切，包括法律与技艺；folklore 强调口头与集体形式。

entries.definition: Recorded personal memories of events; folklore is communal and often older than any witness.
entries.definitionCN: 指记录下来的个人事件记忆；folklore 是集体的，往往比任何见证者更古老。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: folk 'people' plus lore 'teaching' gives 'the teaching of the people'.
normal.cn: folk「民众」加 lore「教导」，得「民众的学问」。

normal.en: The word was coined in 1846 to replace the phrase popular antiquities.
normal.cn: 这个词于 1846 年造出，用来取代「民间古物」这一说法。

normal.en: The family runs folk, lore, folklore, folkloric, folklorist and folkloristics.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 folk、lore、folklore、folkloric、folklorist 与 folkloristics。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: local folklore, rural folklore, folklore collector, folklore and myth.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：地方民俗、乡村民俗、民俗采集者、民俗与神话。

normal.en: The same word now covers memes and message-board stories, because the spread is still anonymous and communal.
normal.cn: 这个词如今也涵盖模因与论坛故事，因为传播仍是匿名且集体的。

abstract.en: Picture a library with no shelves, only voices.
abstract.cn: 想象一座没有书架、只有声音的图书馆。

abstract.en: Picture a story that changes a little each time it is told, and survives by changing.
abstract.cn: 想象一个故事每讲一次就变一点，并靠变化而存活。

abstract.en: Picture a path kept open by the people who retell it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条因不断被复述而保持畅通的路。

examples.en: She collected folklore from fishermen along the whole coast.
examples.cn: 她沿着整条海岸采集渔民的民间故事。

examples.en: The film borrows folklore but invents its own ending.
examples.cn: 这部电影借用了民间传说，却自编了结局。

examples.en: Online folklore spreads faster than any village tale.
examples.cn: 网络民间创作传播得比任何村中故事都快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「folk（民众）+ lore（学问）」——老百姓口口相传的学问

root: 古英语 folc「民众」+ 古英语 lār「教导、学问」；1846 年由威廉·汤姆斯造出，取代「民间古物」。日耳曼语之前的形态均属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one channel: knowledge is passed mouth to ear, and that channel then carries tales, songs, beliefs, craft, a discipline's evidence, one group's tradition, online creation and finally an unverified claim.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一条渠道展开：知识从口传到耳，这条渠道再依次承载故事、歌谣、信念、工艺、学科证据、某群体的传统、网络创作，最后承载未经证实的说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a library with no shelves, only voices passing a story hand to hand without paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座没有书架、只有声音的图书馆，故事不用纸便一手手传下去。

branches.en: THE CHANNEL AND ONE GROUP: the general inheritance, and the specific version kept by a people or trade.
branches.cn: 渠道与某一群体：普遍的继承，以及某个民族或行业保有的特定版本。

branches.en: STORIES: narrative is the part of the inheritance that travels furthest.
branches.cn: 故事：叙事是这份遗产中传播最远的部分。

branches.en: SONGS: melody carries what writing cannot reach.
branches.cn: 歌谣：旋律携带书写触及不到的东西。

branches.en: BELIEF AND OBJECT: superstition explains misfortune, and craft teaches through shape.
branches.cn: 信念与器物：迷信解释不幸，工艺通过形状传授技艺。

branches.en: EVIDENCE, NEW MEDIA, DOUBT: the material becomes a science, then a meme, and finally a word for what cannot be proved.
branches.cn: 证据、新媒介与怀疑：材料先成为科学，再成为模因，最后成为「无法证明之物」的说法。

intro.en: Folklore is a modern compound of two Old English words, so its parts are transparent and its family is built with English suffixes.
intro.cn: folklore 是两个古英语词构成的现代复合词，其成分清晰，词族由英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: No Latin borrowing stands behind this word; both halves are Old English, so no Latin source forms are recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后没有拉丁借词；两半都来自古英语，因此不列拉丁语源形式。

items.example: Folc is the ancestor of folk.
items.exampleCN: folc 是 folk 的祖先形式。

items.example: Lār survives in lore and in learned.
items.exampleCN: lār 存于 lore 与 learned 中。

items.example: Folk can also be an adjective, as in folk music.
items.exampleCN: folk 也可作形容词，如民间音乐。

items.example: Lore often appears in compounds such as plant lore.
items.exampleCN: lore 常出现在植物知识这类复合词中。

items.example: The compound replaced an older phrase.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词取代了更早的说法。

items.example: Folkloric means relating to folklore.
items.exampleCN: folkloric 意为与民俗有关的。

items.example: Folklorist names a collector or scholar.
items.exampleCN: folklorist 指采集者或学者。

items.example: Folkloristics names the discipline itself.
items.exampleCN: folkloristics 指这门学科本身。

items.meaning: deliberately plain and rural in style
items.example: Folksy is often a criticism of manufactured simplicity.
items.exampleCN: folksy 常批评人为制造的朴素。

items.meaning: the customary ways of a people
items.example: Folkways are everyday custom rather than formal law.
items.exampleCN: folkways 指日常习俗，而非正式法律。

definition_zh: 以民间文化传统为研究对象的学科
definition_en: the academic discipline that collects, describes and interprets the traditional culture of ordinary people
core_image: 大学的档案室里放着成排的录音带，标签上写着村庄的名字与年份
scene: 大学的档案室里放着成排的录音带，标签上写着村庄的名字与年份。Collectors who wrote down songs before they disappeared started what we now call folklore studies.
sceneCN: 这里 folklore studies 指「以民间文化传统为研究对象的学科」（第 1 个义项：系统采集与解释民俗的学术领域）；句意为民俗研究始于那些在歌谣消失前把它们记录下来的采集者。可辨识物件：录音带、标签、档案柜、笔记本。

pos.zh: 民俗研究；民俗学（学科名）

collocations.zh: 民俗研究中的田野调查

senses.title: The discipline of studying folk culture
senses.definition: the academic field that collects and interprets the inherited culture of ordinary people
senses.definitionCN: 采集并解释普通民众继承文化的学术领域
senses.example: Folklore studies began with collectors who wrote down songs before they disappeared.
senses.exampleCN: 民俗研究始于那些在歌谣消失前把它们记录下来的采集者。
senses.why: studies marks an organized field, so the phrase names a discipline rather than a pile of stories.
senses.whyCN: studies 标记一个有组织的领域，因此这个短语指学科，而非一堆故事。

senses.title: The history of the discipline
senses.definition: the story of how collectors and scholars turned folk material into a field
senses.definitionCN: 采集者与学者如何把民间材料变成一门学科的历史
senses.example: The course traces folklore studies from the brothers Grimm to modern archives.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程追溯民俗研究从格林兄弟到现代档案的历程。
senses.why: a field defines itself partly by telling the story of its own beginnings.
senses.whyCN: 一个领域部分靠讲述自身起源来定义自己。

senses.title: Fieldwork methods
senses.definition: the practice of recording speech, song and craft in the place where they are used
senses.definitionCN: 在使用现场记录言语、歌谣与工艺的做法
senses.example: Folklore studies relies on long stays in the village, not quick surveys.
senses.exampleCN: 民俗研究依靠在村中久住，而非快速问卷。
senses.why: the material lives in performance, so it must be caught where it is performed.
senses.whyCN: 材料活在表演中，因此必须在它被表演的地方捕捉。

senses.title: The study of oral literature
senses.definition: the analysis of tales, epics and songs as texts that exist without writing
senses.definitionCN: 把故事、史诗与歌谣当作不依赖书写的文本加以分析
senses.example: Folklore studies treats the epic as a performance, not a fixed book.
senses.exampleCN: 民俗研究把这部史诗当作表演，而非固定的书。
senses.why: oral works change in every telling, so the discipline had to invent methods for variation.
senses.whyCN: 口头作品每讲一次都会变化，因此这门学科必须发明处理变异的方法。

senses.title: Folk culture and national identity
senses.definition: the use of folk material to define or defend a nation's sense of itself
senses.definitionCN: 用民间材料界定或捍卫一个民族的自我认同
senses.example: Nineteenth-century folklore studies helped build national identity.
senses.exampleCN: 十九世纪的民俗研究参与了民族认同的建构。
senses.why: collected songs can be made into a national heritage, and the discipline has been used for that purpose.
senses.whyCN: 采集来的歌谣可以被造成民族遗产，这门学科也曾被用于此目的。

senses.title: Research on material folk culture
senses.definition: the study of tools, buildings, cloth and food as carriers of inherited knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 把工具、建筑、织物与食物当作传承知识的载体来研究
senses.example: Folklore studies examines barn design as inherited engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 民俗研究把谷仓设计当作传承的工程知识来考察。
senses.why: the field widened from words to things once it admitted craft as lore.
senses.whyCN: 当这门学科承认工艺也是学问，它的范围便从言语扩展到器物。

senses.title: The study of performance and ritual
senses.definition: the analysis of festivals, rites and storytelling as events rather than texts
senses.definitionCN: 把节庆、仪式与讲故事当作事件而非文本加以分析
senses.example: Folklore studies recorded how the procession actually moved.
senses.exampleCN: 民俗研究记录了游行实际如何行进。
senses.why: performance is where a tradition is remade, not merely repeated.
senses.whyCN: 表演是传统被重造之处，而不只是被重复之处。

senses.title: Public folklore and applied practice
senses.definition: the use of the discipline in museums, festivals and community projects
senses.definitionCN: 在博物馆、节庆与社区项目中使用这门学科
senses.example: Public folklore studies now advise museums on whose story to tell.
senses.exampleCN: 公共民俗研究如今为博物馆建议该讲谁的故事。
senses.why: a discipline that only archives its material is soon asked what it is for.
senses.whyCN: 一门只把材料归档的学科，很快就会被问它有什么用。

intro.en: Folklore studies joins the coined word folklore, from Old English folc 'people' and lār 'teaching', with studies, from Latin studium 'eagerness, study'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: folklore studies 由造出的 folklore（古英语 folc「民众」加 lār「教导」）与 studies（拉丁 studium「热忱、钻研」）组合而成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Folc meant 'people' and lār meant 'teaching'. Their pre-Germanic shapes are reconstructed rather than witnessed.
items.cn: folc 意为「民众」，lār 意为「教导」。它们在日耳曼语之前的形态属重构形式，并无实际书证。

items.en: William Thoms coined folklore in 1846 to name the study of popular antiquities, so the material and the field were named together.
items.cn: 威廉·汤姆斯于 1846 年造出 folklore，用来命名对民间古物的研究，材料与领域因此同时得名。

items.en: Studium meant 'eagerness, painstaking application', from studere 'to be eager, to strive'; English study and student descend from it.
items.cn: studium 意为「热忱、刻苦钻研」，出自 studere「热切、努力」；英语 study 与 student 由此而来。

items.en: The phrase folklore studies took its present form in the twentieth century, when universities created chairs and journals for the field.
items.cn: folklore studies 这一短语在二十世纪定形，当时大学为该领域设立教席与刊物。

items.en: The field now includes material culture, performance, public folklore and digital creation, so the plural studies marks several methods rather than one.
items.cn: 该领域如今包括物质文化、表演、公共民俗与数字创作，复数 studies 因此标记多种方法，而非单一方法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): no single first use of the exact phrase is recorded, and the pre-Germanic shapes of folc and lār are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这一确切短语没有单一的最早书证；folc 与 lār 在日耳曼语之前的形态属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same compound and its academic family; group two holds neighbouring disciplines.
note.cn: 第一组是同一复合词及其学术词族的成员；第二组是相邻学科。

entries.definition: The stories and customs themselves; folklore studies is the discipline that examines them.
entries.definitionCN: 指故事与习俗本身；folklore studies 是考察它们的学科。

entries.definition: A practitioner of the field; the phrase names the field, not its member.
entries.definitionCN: 指该领域的从业者；短语指领域，而非其成员。

entries.definition: A formal synonym for the discipline, stressing method rather than the material.
entries.definitionCN: 该学科的正式同义词，强调方法而非材料。

entries.definition: The comparative study of peoples and cultures; folklore studies focuses on inherited expressive forms.
entries.definitionCN: 指对各民族与文化的比较研究；民俗研究聚焦于传承的表达形式。

entries.definition: The study of human societies as a whole, including but not limited to folk material.
entries.definitionCN: 指对整个人类社会的研究，包含但不限于民间材料。

entries.definition: The descriptive recording of a way of life, often by long residence; it is a method used within folklore studies.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某种生活方式的描述性记录，常靠长期居住；它是民俗研究中使用的方法。

entries.definition: The study of contemporary culture and power; folklore studies is older and tied to inherited forms.
entries.definitionCN: 指对当代文化与权力的研究；民俗研究更古老，且与传承形式相连。

entries.definition: The study of how the past is conserved and presented; folklore studies begins with collection rather than preservation policy.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究过去如何被保存与展示；民俗研究从采集而非保存政策开始。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: folklore is the material; studies is the organized look at it.
normal.cn: folklore 是材料；studies 是对它的有组织考察。

normal.en: study and student come from Latin studere 'to strive', so the phrase names effort as well as subject matter.
normal.cn: study 与 student 来自拉丁 studere「努力」，因此这个短语既指材料，也指投入。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: department of folklore studies, comparative folklore studies, fieldwork in folklore studies.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：民俗研究系、比较民俗研究、民俗研究中的田野调查。

normal.en: The plural studies signals several methods, not several folk cultures.
normal.cn: 复数 studies 标记多种方法，而非多种民间文化。

normal.en: The discipline's founders were collectors, which is why archives and recordings remain central.
normal.cn: 这门学科的创始人是采集者，因此档案与录音至今仍是核心。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of tapes labelled by village and year.
abstract.cn: 想象一架录音带，按村庄与年份贴标签。

abstract.en: Picture a scholar learning a song by sitting through it many times.
abstract.cn: 想象一位学者靠反复坐听来学会一首歌。

abstract.en: Picture a field that began as a box of curiosities and became a method.
abstract.cn: 想象一个领域从一箱奇珍变成一套方法。

examples.en: She holds a chair in folklore studies at the university.
examples.cn: 她在大学担任民俗研究教席。

examples.en: Folklore studies changed how museums present rural life.
examples.cn: 民俗研究改变了博物馆呈现乡村生活的方式。

examples.en: His fieldwork became a standard model in folklore studies.
examples.cn: 他的田野工作成为民俗研究的标准范例。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「folklore（民俗）+ studies（研究）」——专门研究老百姓传下来的东西

root: folklore 由古英语 folc「民众」与 lār「教导」构成，1846 年造词；studies 来自拉丁 studium「热忱、钻研」，出自 studere「努力」。更早形态均属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one field: a body of inherited culture becomes an object of methodical study, and that study then has a history, a fieldwork, a literature, a politics, a material side and a public face.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个领域展开：一整套传承文化成为系统研究的对象，这门研究再依次拥有历史、田野方法、口头文学、民族政治、物质面与公共面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shelf of tapes labelled by village and year, each one a voice kept after the singer is gone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架按村庄与年份标注的录音带，每一盘都是歌者离去后留下的声音。

branches.en: THE FIELD AND ITS OBJECTS: the discipline begins with words and extends to tools and buildings.
branches.cn: 领域与其对象：学科从言语开始，扩展到工具与建筑。

branches.en: THE STORY OF ITSELF: a field explains its methods by narrating its founders.
branches.cn: 自身的故事：一个领域通过叙述其创始人来解释自己的方法。

branches.en: THE METHOD: long residence is how performance is caught before it vanishes.
branches.cn: 方法：长期居住是赶在表演消失前捕捉它的方式。

branches.en: THE TEXT WITHOUT WRITING: oral works must be analysed as changing performances.
branches.cn: 无需书写的文本：口头作品必须作为变化的表演来分析。

branches.en: IDENTITY, PERFORMANCE, PUBLIC: collected material can build a nation, stage a rite or advise a museum.
branches.cn: 认同、表演、公共：采集的材料可以建构民族、上演仪式或为博物馆建言。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Germanic compound with a Latin noun of effort, so the family splits into folk words and study words.
intro.cn: 这个短语把一个日耳曼语复合词与一个拉丁语「努力」名词连接起来，词族因此分为民间词与学习词两支。

latinIntro.en: Latin studium and studere stand behind studies, study, student and studious; the folklore half remains Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 studium 与 studere 是 studies、study、student 与 studious 的来源；folklore 那一半仍属日耳曼语。

items.example: Folc is the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: folc 是复合词的前一半。

items.example: Lār is the second half.
items.exampleCN: lār 是后一半。

items.example: The material half of the phrase is recent.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语的材料一半是近代造词。

items.example: The verb supplies the effort behind study.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供 study 背后的努力义。

items.example: Studium became English study.
items.exampleCN: studium 成为英语 study。

items.example: Study can be a verb or a noun.
items.exampleCN: study 可作动词或名词。

items.example: The plural marks a discipline rather than one act.
items.exampleCN: 复数标记一门学科，而非一次行为。

items.example: Student is the person who does the studying.
items.exampleCN: student 是从事学习的人。

items.example: Studious describes the disposition.
items.exampleCN: studious 描述这种性情。

items.example: The -istics form competes with the plural studies.
items.exampleCN: -istics 形式与复数 studies 并用。

definition_zh: 一个文化的神话总体；神话学；也指被广泛相信却不实的观念体系
definition_en: the body of myths belonging to a culture, the study of such myths, and a widely held but unfounded set of beliefs
core_image: 神庙的壁画上画着一位持雷的神，旁边的铭文讲他如何生出大地
scene: 神庙的壁画上画着一位持雷的神，旁边的铭文讲他如何生出大地。Greek mythology gives the storm god a spear and a short temper.
sceneCN: 这里 mythology 指「一个文化的神话总体」（第 1 个义项：关于神祇与起源的故事集合）；句意为希腊神话赋予这位风暴之神一柄长矛和急躁的脾气。可辨识物件：壁画、雷、长矛、铭文、神庙。

pos.zh: 被广泛相信的不实观念体系

senses.title: A culture's body of myths
senses.definition: the whole collection of stories a society tells about gods, heroes and origins
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会关于神祇、英雄与起源的全部故事集合
senses.example: Greek mythology gives the storm god a spear and a short temper.
senses.exampleCN: 希腊神话赋予风暴之神一柄长矛和急躁的脾气。
senses.why: mythos meant a told story and -logia meant an account, so the word first names a body of stories told together.
senses.whyCN: mythos 指被讲述的故事，-logia 指叙述，因此这个词先指被一起讲述的故事总体。

senses.title: The myths of one particular people
senses.definition: the specific myth system of a named culture, such as Greek, Norse or Egyptian
senses.definitionCN: 某个具名文化的特定神话体系，如希腊、北欧或埃及
senses.example: Norse mythology ends with a fire that consumes the world.
senses.exampleCN: 北欧神话以一场吞噬世界的大火结束。
senses.why: each people organizes its stories into a recognisable system with its own gods.
senses.whyCN: 每个民族把自己的故事组织成可辨认的体系，各有其神。

senses.title: The scholarly study of myth
senses.definition: the academic analysis of myths and their meanings, functions and structures
senses.definitionCN: 对神话及其意义、功能与结构进行的学术分析
senses.example: Comparative mythology looks for shared patterns across continents.
senses.exampleCN: 比较神话学在各大洲寻找共同模式。
senses.why: the same -logia that names a field in other disciplines here names the study of myth.
senses.whyCN: -logia 在其他学科中标记领域，这里标记对神话的研究。

senses.title: A widely believed set of ideas
senses.titleCN: 被广泛相信的观念体系
senses.definition: a system of beliefs that a group treats as obvious though it is not proven
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体视为理所当然、却未经证明的信念体系
senses.example: The mythology of endless growth shaped the whole plan.
senses.exampleCN: 无限增长的信念体系塑造了整个计划。
senses.why: modern writers borrowed the word for secular faiths that work like myths.
senses.whyCN: 现代作者借用这个词来指像神话般运作的世俗信仰。

senses.title: A false story people repeat
senses.titleCN: 被反复传播的不实说法（贬义）
senses.definition: used dismissively of an unfounded claim that circulates as if it were fact
senses.definitionCN: 轻蔑地指一种被当作事实传播的无据说法
senses.example: The story that he invented the machine is pure mythology.
senses.exampleCN: 说他发明了那台机器的说法纯属神话。
senses.why: once a story is doubted, mythology becomes a word for comfortable untruth.
senses.whyCN: 一旦故事受到怀疑，mythology 就变成「令人安心的假话」之词。

senses.title: The gods and heroes in a myth system
senses.titleCN: 神话体系中的神祇与英雄
senses.definition: the characters that populate a myth system and carry its values
senses.definitionCN: 填充神话体系并承载其价值观的角色
senses.example: The mythology of the city is crowded with rival patron gods.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的神话挤满了相互竞争的守护神。
senses.why: a system needs actors, and gods and heroes are the actors of myth.
senses.whyCN: 体系需要行动者，而神祇与英雄正是神话的行动者。

senses.title: A creation story
senses.definition: the narrative that explains how the world, life or a people began
senses.definitionCN: 解释世界、生命或一个民族如何开始的叙事
senses.example: Their mythology begins with a bird that drops a grain of sand.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的创世神话始于一只鸟丢下一粒沙。
senses.why: origins are the question myths exist to answer, so creation is their central episode.
senses.whyCN: 起源是神话存在所要回答的问题，因此创世是其核心情节。

senses.title: Recurring motifs and archetypes
senses.definition: the repeated images and patterns that move between myth systems
senses.definitionCN: 在不同神话体系之间流动的重复意象与模式
senses.example: The dying-and-rising god is a common mythology motif.
senses.exampleCN: 死而复生的神是常见的神话母题。
senses.why: comparison needs units smaller than a whole system, and motifs supply them.
senses.whyCN: 比较研究需要小于整个体系的单位，母题正好提供。

senses.title: Myths retold in art and literature
senses.titleCN: 神话在文学艺术中的再创作
senses.definition: the reuse of mythic material by later writers, painters and composers
senses.definitionCN: 后世作家、画家与作曲家对神话材料的再利用
senses.example: Modern opera keeps the old mythology but changes the ending.
senses.exampleCN: 现代歌剧保留古老神话，却改写了结局。
senses.why: myths survive by being retold, so each retelling adds a new layer to the word.
senses.whyCN: 神话靠被重讲而存活，每次重讲都为这个词添上新一层。

intro.en: Mythology comes from Greek mythologia 'a telling of legends', from mythos 'word, story' plus -logia 'an account, a study', through Late Latin and French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mythology 经晚期拉丁语与法语来自希腊 mythologia「讲述传说」，由 mythos「话语、故事」加 -logia「叙述、研究」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mythos meant 'word, speech, tale', without the modern implication of falsehood; the contrast with logos as 'reasoned account' came later.
items.cn: mythos 意为「话语、言说、故事」，起初不含现代「虚假」之意；它与表示「理性叙述」的 logos 的对立是后来才形成的。

items.en: The suffix -logia came from logos 'word, reason' and named an account or study of a subject.
items.cn: 后缀 -logia 出自 logos「言词、理性」，指对某一主题的叙述或研究。

items.en: Mythologia named the telling of legends and the body of such tales, not yet a science of them.
items.cn: mythologia 指传说的讲述与这类故事的整体，尚未指研究它们的科学。

items.en: Late Latin mythologia and French mythologie carried the word into English, where it named both a collection of myths and their study.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 mythologia 与法语 mythologie 把词带入英语，同时指神话集合与对它的研究。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word was extended to secular belief systems and finally to any unfounded story.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个词被扩展到世俗信念体系，最终指任何无据的说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest use of the dismissive sense is dated only approximately, and the details of the Greek formation are reconstructed from surviving texts.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：贬义的最早用法只有约略年代；希腊语构词细节是根据传世文本重构出来的。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the Greek mythos stem; group two holds narrative and belief terms often confused with it.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊 mythos 词干的词；第二组是常与之混淆的叙事与信念词。

entries.definition: A single sacred or traditional narrative; mythology is the whole body or the study of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指单则神圣或传统叙事；mythology 指整体或对它的研究。

entries.definition: Means 'of myth' or 'like myth', often used of larger-than-life figures.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「神话的」或「神话般的」，常用于超凡人物。

entries.definition: Relating to mythology as a system or field rather than to one story.
entries.definitionCN: 指与作为体系或学科的神话学有关，而非单则故事。

entries.definition: To turn a person or event into myth, or to interpret something mythically.
entries.definitionCN: 指把人或事件神话化，或以神话方式解释某物。

entries.definition: A story about a person or place, told as if it happened; it need not involve gods.
entries.definitionCN: 指关于某人或某地、仿佛真有其事的故事；不必涉及神祇。

entries.definition: Inherited knowledge of any kind; mythology is a particular sacred or origin-focused part of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何传承知识；mythology 是其中专注神圣或起源的特定部分。

entries.definition: All the gods of a people taken together, or a temple for them; it is a part of mythology, not the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个民族全部神祇的集合，或供奉他们的神庙；它是神话的一部分，而非全部。

entries.definition: The whole inherited culture of ordinary people; mythology is its most sacred and origin-focused strand.
entries.definitionCN: 指普通民众继承的整体文化；mythology 是其中最具神圣性与起源关切的一支。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: mythos 'story' plus -logia 'account' gives 'an account of stories'.
normal.cn: mythos「故事」加 -logia「叙述」，得「对故事的叙述」。

normal.en: The family runs myth, mythic, mythical, mythological, mythologist and mythologize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 myth、mythic、mythical、mythological、mythologist 与 mythologize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: Greek mythology, ancient mythology, comparative mythology, popular mythology.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：希腊神话、古代神话、比较神话学、大众流行的错误观念。

normal.en: mythos did not originally mean 'false'; the modern dismissal came much later.
normal.cn: mythos 起初并不表示「虚假」；现代的贬义是后来才有的。

normal.en: A mythology is a system; a myth is one story inside it.
normal.cn: mythology 是一个体系；myth 是体系中的一则故事。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of painted gods, each one explaining a part of the weather.
abstract.cn: 想象一面画满神祇的墙，每一位都在解释一部分天气。

abstract.en: Picture a story that a whole city agrees to remember.
abstract.cn: 想象一个整座城市都同意记住的故事。

abstract.en: Picture a comforting belief that nobody has bothered to test.
abstract.cn: 想象一个无人费心去检验的安慰性信念。

examples.en: The course compares creation stories in three mythologies.
examples.cn: 这门课程比较三种神话中的创世故事。

examples.en: The mythology of the frontier still shapes political speech.
examples.cn: 边疆神话至今仍塑造政治话语。

examples.en: His biography separates the man from the mythology around him.
examples.cn: 他的传记把本人与围绕他的神话区分开来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「myth（神话）+ ology（学问）」——讲神的故事，也研究这些故事

root: 希腊 mythos「话语、故事」+ -logia「叙述、研究」（出自 logos「言词、理性」）→ 希腊 mythologia → 晚期拉丁 mythologia → 法语 mythologie → 英语 mythology。mythos 原不含「虚假」义。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one telling: a people gathers its stories about gods and origins, and that gathering is then read as a system, a science, a secular faith, a false tale, a cast of gods, a creation scene, a motif and a source for art.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一次讲述展开：一个民族把关于神祇与起源的故事聚拢，这个聚拢再依次被读作体系、学科、世俗信仰、假话、神祇群、创世场景、母题与艺术素材。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a temple wall where every painted god explains one part of the weather.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面神庙墙壁，每位画中的神都解释一部分天气。

branches.en: THE WHOLE AND ONE PEOPLE'S VERSION: a collection of stories, and the specific system a culture owns.
branches.cn: 整体与某一民族的版本：故事集合，以及一个文化所拥有的特定体系。

branches.en: THE STUDY: the same word names the disciplined look at myth.
branches.cn: 研究：同一个词也指对神话的系统考察。

branches.en: ACTORS AND ORIGINS: gods fill the system, and creation explains why there is a world at all.
branches.cn: 角色与起源：神祇填充体系，创世解释世界为何存在。

branches.en: UNITS AND REUSE: motifs travel between systems, and artists retell them with new endings.
branches.cn: 单位与再利用：母题在体系间流动，艺术家以新结局重讲它们。

branches.en: SECULAR FAITH AND FALSE STORY: when the gods leave, the word can still name a belief people refuse to test.
branches.cn: 世俗信仰与假故事：当神祇离场，这个词仍可指人们拒绝检验的信念。

intro.en: Mythology is two Greek elements joined, one naming a story and one naming an account, and both build large English families.
intro.cn: mythology 由两个希腊成分组合而成，一个指故事，一个指叙述，两者都构成庞大的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Greek mythos and -logia reached English through Late Latin mythologia and French mythologie, so the Latin forms are borrowings from Greek rather than native Latin words.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 mythos 与 -logia 经晚期拉丁 mythologia 与法语 mythologie 进入英语，因此这些拉丁形式是从希腊语借入的，而非拉丁本族词。

items.example: Mythos named a story before it implied a false one.
items.exampleCN: mythos 先指故事，后来才含虚假之意。

items.example: The suffix names fields from biology to theology.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名从生物学到神学的众多领域。

items.example: Logos is the root behind the suffix.
items.exampleCN: logos 是该后缀背后的词根。

items.example: The Greek noun already covered both telling and collecting.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词已同时涵盖讲述与汇集。

items.structure: mythologia, through Late Latin and French
items.meaning: a body of myths; their study
items.example: English merged the two senses in one word.
items.exampleCN: 英语把两个义项并入一个词。

items.example: Myth is the countable unit inside mythology.
items.exampleCN: myth 是 mythology 内部的可数单位。

items.example: Mythic means relating to or like myth.
items.exampleCN: mythic 意为与神话有关或像神话的。

items.example: Mythological points at the system or the study.
items.exampleCN: mythological 指向体系或学科。

items.example: Mythologist names the scholar.
items.exampleCN: mythologist 指学者。

items.example: Mythologize means to turn into myth.
items.exampleCN: mythologize 意为使成为神话。

latinEntries.structure: mythologia, mythologiae (f., first declension; Latin borrowing from Greek)
mythicus, mythica, mythicum (adjective, Late Latin from Greek mythikos)
mythos (m., second declension; Latin borrowing from Greek)
